lessons.title: Family Members and Descriptions
lessons.description: Essential family vocabulary, possessive adjectives and how to describe people in French.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for family members (la famille)
Use être for personality traits and avoir for physical features
Apply adjective agreement: -e for feminine, -s/-es for plural
Build extended descriptions using connectives like mais, aussi and cependant
method_card.title: Family Members and Descriptions
method_card.content:
This lesson covers family members, physical appearance and personality adjectives in French. Two key grammar rules underpin everything: use être for personality and permanent characteristics, and avoir for physical features like hair and eyes.

FrançaisEnglish
le père / la mèrefather / mother
le frère / la sœurbrother / sister
le grand-père / la grand-mèregrandfather / grandmother
l'oncle / la tanteuncle / aunt
le beau-père / la belle-mèrestepfather / stepmother
le fils / la filleson / daughter
grand(e)tall / big
petit(e)small / short
minceslim
aîné(e) / cadet(te)older / younger
sympa / sympathiquenice, friendly
drôle / amusant(e)funny
travailleur/eusehardworking
paresseux/euselazy
gentil(le)kind

Grammar focus: être vs avoir for descriptions. Use être for personality and permanent traits: Il est gentil (He is kind). Use avoir for hair and eyes: Il a les yeux bleus (He has blue eyes), Elle a les cheveux longs (She has long hair). In French, eye and hair colour adjectives follow the noun.

Adjectives must agree with the noun they describe. Most adjectives add -e for feminine and -s for plural (or -es for feminine plural). Some are irregular: travailleur → travailleuse, paresseux → paresseuse, gentil → gentille.

Model paragraph: Ma mère est grande et mince. Elle a les cheveux longs et bruns et les yeux verts. Elle est très gentille et travailleuse. (My mother is tall and slim. She has long brown hair and green eyes. She is very kind and hardworking.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — family descriptions appear across speaking, listening, reading and writing every year

lessons.title: Friendships and Qualities
lessons.description: Talking about friends, describing qualities and using the near future tense in French.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for describing a good friend
Master adjective agreement for masculine and feminine forms
Use reflexive verbs s'entendre bien avec and se disputer avec correctly
Form comparative sentences using plus ... que and moins ... que
method_card.title: Friendships and Qualities
method_card.content:
This lesson covers how to describe friendships and the qualities of a good friend. Key structures include using être for personality descriptions, reflexive verbs such as s'entendre bien avec (to get on well with) and se disputer avec (to argue with), and making comparisons using plus ... que (more ... than).

FrenchEnglish
un ami / une amiea friend (m/f)
un bon ami / une bonne amiea good friend (m/f)
honnêtehonest
fidèleloyal, faithful
drôlefunny
gentil / gentillekind (m/f)
sympa (invariable)nice, friendly
bavard / bavardechatty (m/f)
généreux / généreusegenerous (m/f)
s'entendre bien avecto get on well with
se disputer avecto argue with
faire confiance àto trust
plus ... quemore ... than
moins ... queless ... than
à mon avisin my opinion

Grammar focus: adjective agreement and reflexive verbs. Adjectives must agree with the noun they describe. Most adjectives add -e for feminine: fidèle → fidèle (no change — already ends in -e), honnête → honnête (no change). Others change form: gentil → gentille, généreux → généreuse, bavard → bavarde. The adjective sympa is invariable (never changes). Reflexive verbs like s'entendre and se disputer use reflexive pronouns: je m'entends, tu t'entends, il/elle s'entend, nous nous entendons.

Comparatives: Use plus + adjective + que for 'more ... than', and moins + adjective + que for 'less ... than'. Remember the adjective still agrees: Elle est plus généreuse que moi.

Model paragraph: À mon avis, un bon ami doit être honnête et fidèle. Je m'entends bien avec ma meilleure amie parce qu'elle est plus drôle que les autres. (In my opinion, a good friend must be honest and loyal. I get on well with my best friend because she is funnier than the others.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — friendships and personal qualities appear across speaking, listening, reading and writing every year

lessons.title: Relationships, Marriage and Future Plans
lessons.description: Discussing relationships, marriage and future plans using the conditional tense in French.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for relationships and future plans
Master the future tense by adding endings to the infinitive (or irregular stem)
Use the conditional (je voudrais, je préférerais) to express wishes politely
Form si-clauses using si + present tense followed by the future tense
method_card.title: Relationships, Marriage and Future Plans
method_card.content:
This lesson covers relationships, attitudes towards marriage and cohabitation, and how to talk about future plans. Key structures include the future tense (je me marierai — I will get married) and the conditional (je voudrais — I would like) to express wishes and hypothetical plans.

FrenchEnglish
se marierto get married
le mariagemarriage / wedding
vivre ensembleto live together
le partenaire / la partenairepartner (m/f)
une relationa relationship
tomber amoureux/amoureuseto fall in love
rester célibataireto stay single
l'avenir (m)the future
avoir des enfantsto have children
l'engagement (m)commitment
important(e)important
à mon avisin my opinion
plus tardlater / in the future
si + present → futureif … (si-clause structure)

Grammar focus: the future tense and conditional. The future tense is formed by adding endings to the infinitive: -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont. For example: je me marierai (I will get married), nous aurons des enfants (we will have children). Some verbs have irregular future stems: être → ser-, avoir → aur-, vouloir → voudr-, pouvoir → pourr-, aller → ir-. The conditional uses the same stems but with imperfect endings: je voudrais (I would like), je préférerais (I would prefer).

Si-clauses: Use si + present tense in the condition, and the future tense in the result: Si je rencontre la bonne personne, je me marierai. (If I meet the right person, I will get married.)

Model paragraph: À mon avis, le mariage est très important. Plus tard, je voudrais me marier et avoir des enfants. Si je rencontre la bonne personne, je serai très heureux/heureuse. (In my opinion, marriage is very important. Later, I would like to get married and have children. If I meet the right person, I will be very happy.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — relationships and future plans appear in speaking, writing, listening and reading tasks every year

lessons.title: Healthy Living and Lifestyle
lessons.description: Health, fitness and lifestyle vocabulary with il faut, reflexive verbs and exam phrases.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for healthy and unhealthy habits
Use il faut and il est important de + infinitive to give advice
Conjugate devoir to say what someone must do
Build extended sentences about lifestyle using connectives
method_card.title: Healthy Living and Lifestyle
method_card.content:
This lesson covers healthy and unhealthy habits, diet and exercise. Key structures include devoir (must), il faut (one must / you have to) and il est important de (it is important to), all followed by the infinitive, to give advice about health.

FrenchEnglish
mener une vie saineto lead a healthy life
mener une vie malsaineto lead an unhealthy life
se nourrir sainementto eat healthily
faire de l'exerciceto do exercise
faire du sportto do sport
bien dormirto sleep well
fumerto smoke
boire de l'alcoolto drink alcohol
les matières grassesfatty foods / fat
les légumes (m)vegetables
les fruits (m)fruit
les sucreries (f)sweets / sugary foods
sain / sainehealthy (m/f)
malsain / malsaineunhealthy (m/f)
équilibré / équilibréebalanced (m/f)

Grammar focus: devoir, il faut and il est important de + infinitive. These three structures are used to give advice or say what someone must do. Devoir is conjugated to match the subject: je dois (I must), tu dois (you must), il/elle doit (he/she must), nous devons, vous devez, ils/elles doivent. Il faut and il est important de are impersonal and never change. All three are followed by an infinitive: Il faut manger sainement. (You must eat healthily.)

Model paragraph: Pour mener une vie saine, il faut faire de l'exercice régulièrement et il est important de se nourrir sainement. On ne doit pas fumer ni boire trop d'alcool. (To lead a healthy life, you must exercise regularly and it is important to eat healthily. One must not smoke or drink too much alcohol.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — healthy lifestyle and giving advice appear across all four papers every year

model_answers: Si je mangeais moins de malbouffe et faisais plus de sport, je serais en meilleure santé et j'aurais plus d'énergie.

gaps.rule: Si clause + imperfect tense (conditional sentence type 2)

wrong.manges: manges is the present tense. For a hypothetical condition (if you were to eat...), use the imperfect: mangeais.
wrong.mangeras: mangeras is the future tense. In a type 2 conditional, the si clause uses the imperfect, not the future.

gaps.correct_explain: mangeais is the imperfect of manger for tu. In a type 2 conditional, the si clause uses the imperfect tense.

gaps.rule: Main clause — conditional of être (tu form)

wrong.es: es is the present tense of être. After a si + imperfect clause, use the conditional: serais.
wrong.étais: étais is the imperfect of être. The main clause needs the conditional: serais, not the imperfect.

gaps.correct_explain: serais is the conditional of être for tu. The main clause of a type 2 conditional uses the conditional tense.

gaps.rule: Main clause — conditional of dormir (tu form)

wrong.dors: dors is the present tense. In the main clause of a type 2 conditional, use the conditional: dormirais.
wrong.dormiras: dormiras is the future tense. The conditional (would sleep) is dormirais, not the future.

gaps.correct_explain: dormirais is the conditional of dormir for tu. Regular -ir verbs add conditional endings to the infinitive stem.

gaps.rule: Il faut + infinitive for impersonal obligation

wrong.est: il est starts the phrase il est important de, but that phrase needs de before the infinitive, not a direct infinitive.
wrong.dois: dois is the je or tu form of devoir. The phrase here is impersonal — use il faut, not il dois.

gaps.correct_explain: faut completes the impersonal phrase il faut (you must / one must), which is always followed by an infinitive.

wrong.fait du sport: fait du sport is a conjugated verb form. After il faut you always use the infinitive: faire du sport.
wrong.faisant du sport: faisant du sport is the present participle, not the infinitive. After il faut you need the infinitive: faire.

gaps.rule: Devoir — negation: ne ... pas around the conjugated verb

wrong.doit: doit is the il/elle form. The subject is je → dois.
wrong.faut: il faut is impersonal. Here the subject is je, so conjugate devoir: je ne dois pas.

gaps.correct_explain: dois again for je. The negation goes around the conjugated verb: je ne dois pas + infinitive.

lessons.title: Food, Drink and Mealtimes

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for food, drink and the three main meals

method_card.title: Food, Drink and Mealtimes
method_card.content:
This lesson covers food and drink vocabulary, the names of the three main meals, and how to express preferences. A key grammar point is the partitive article, used when saying you eat or drink 'some' of something.

FrançaisEnglish
le petit-déjeunerbreakfast
le déjeunerlunch
le dînerdinner
le painbread
le fromagecheese
le pouletchicken
les légumes (m pl)vegetables
les fruits (m pl)fruit
la viandemeat
la saladesalad
les frites (f pl)chips / fries
l'eau (f)water
le jus d'orangeorange juice
manger / boireto eat / to drink
délicieux / délicieusedelicious

Grammar focus: the partitive article. Use the partitive article to say you eat or drink 'some' of something. The form depends on the gender and first letter of the noun: du (masculine) — Je mange du pain; de la (feminine) — Je bois de la limonade; de l' (before a vowel or silent h) — Je mange de l'agneau; des (plural) — Je mange des frites. After a negative, all forms become simply de: Je ne mange pas de viande.

Model paragraph: Au petit-déjeuner, je mange du pain grillé et je bois du jus d'orange. J'aime beaucoup les fruits mais je déteste les légumes. Je préfère le dîner parce que toute la famille mange ensemble. (At breakfast, I eat toast and drink orange juice. I really like fruit but I hate vegetables. I prefer dinner because the whole family eats together.)

method_card.title: Body Parts, Illness and Wellbeing
method_card.content:
This lesson covers parts of the body, illness and wellbeing. The key structure for saying where it hurts is j'ai mal à + the body part. Because à contracts with le and les, you must use the correct contracted form.

FrançaisEnglish
la têtehead
le dosback
le ventrestomach / belly
la gorgethroat
la jambeleg
le brasarm
le piedfoot
l'oreille (f)ear
les yeux (m pl)eyes
j'ai mal à la têteI have a headache
j'ai mal au dosmy back hurts
j'ai mal aux dentsI have toothache
la fièvrefever / temperature
se sentir bien / malto feel well / unwell
se reposerto rest

Grammar focus: j'ai mal à + contractions. À + le → au: j'ai mal au dos. À + la → à la: j'ai mal à la gorge. À + l' → à l': j'ai mal à l'oreille. À + les → aux: j'ai mal aux pieds. Never use a possessive (mon/ma) — French always uses the definite article with body parts.

Model paragraph: Je ne me sens pas bien aujourd'hui. J'ai mal à la gorge et j'ai de la fièvre. Le médecin m'a conseillé de me reposer et de boire beaucoup d'eau. (I don't feel well today. I have a sore throat and a temperature. The doctor advised me to rest and drink plenty of water.)

Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

lessons.title: Sport and Staying Active
lessons.description: Sports vocabulary, jouer à vs faire de, past tense with être, and sporting events.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for sports and physical activities

method_card.title: Sport and Staying Active
method_card.content:
This lesson covers sports vocabulary, fitness and healthy living in French. A key grammar rule divides sports into two groups: use faire de + article for sports you 'do' (generally individual or non-team sports), and jouer à + article for sports you 'play' (generally team or ball sports).

FrançaisEnglish
faire du véloto cycle / go cycling
faire de la natationto swim / go swimming
faire de l'athlétismeto do athletics
faire de la gymto do gymnastics/gym
jouer au foot(ball)to play football
jouer au tennisto play tennis
jouer au basketto play basketball
jouer au rugbyto play rugby
rester en formeto stay fit / keep fit
se détendreto relax
tous les joursevery day
une fois par semaineonce a week
rarementrarely
j'ai jouéI played (perfect tense)
j'ai faitI did / I went (perfect tense)

Grammar focus: faire de vs jouer à. With faire, the article contracts: faire du vélo (du = de + le), faire de la natation, faire de l'athlétisme. With jouer, use à which also contracts: jouer au foot (au = à + le), jouer à la pétanque. For negation: Je ne fais pas de natation (de replaces du/de la after negation).

Perfect tense with avoir: To talk about past sport, use avoir + past participle: j'ai joué au foot (I played football), j'ai fait du vélo (I went cycling). Add a time phrase to anchor it: le week-end dernier (last weekend), hier (yesterday).

Model paragraph: Je fais de la natation deux fois par semaine et je joue au tennis le week-end. Le week-end dernier, j'ai joué au foot avec mes amis. C'était super. (I swim twice a week and I play tennis at the weekend. Last weekend I played football with my friends. It was great.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — sport and health appear across all papers every year

method_card.title: School Subjects and Opinions
method_card.content:
This lesson covers school subjects and how to express opinions and comparisons about them in French. You will use key vocabulary for les matières alongside opinion phrases and comparative structures.

FrançaisEnglish
les mathématiques (les maths)mathematics / maths
le françaisFrench
l'anglaisEnglish
l'histoire-géohistory and geography
les sciencesscience
l'informatiquecomputing / ICT
l'EPS (éducation physique et sportive)PE
les arts plastiquesart
la musiquemusic
utileuseful
ennuyeux / ennuyeuseboring
intéressant(e)interesting
difficiledifficult
facileeasy
être fort(e) ento be good at
être nul(le) ento be bad/rubbish at

Grammar focus: comparatives and opinion structures. Use plus + adjective + que (more ... than) or moins + adjective + que (less ... than) to compare subjects: Les maths sont plus difficiles que le français. (Maths is more difficult than French.) Use je suis fort(e) en to say you are good at a subject and je suis nul(le) en to say you are bad at it. Give reasons with parce que c'est + adjective: J'aime l'histoire parce que c'est intéressant.

Model paragraph: Ma matière préférée, c'est les sciences parce que c'est utile et intéressant. Je suis fort en sciences mais je suis nul en arts plastiques. À mon avis, les maths sont plus difficiles que l'anglais. (My favourite subject is science because it is useful and interesting. I am good at science but I am bad at art. In my opinion, maths is more difficult than English.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — school subjects, opinions and comparisons appear across all four papers every year

method_card.title: School Life, Rules and Uniform
method_card.content:
This lesson covers school life, daily routine and school rules in French. The key grammar structures are modal rule expressions and reflexive verbs for the school day routine.

FrançaisEnglish
le lycée / le collègesecondary school / lower secondary
la salle de classeclassroom
la bibliothèquelibrary
la cantinecanteen / dining hall
le terrain de sportsports field
il est interdit de + inf.it is forbidden to
on doit + inf.one must / we must
on ne doit pas + inf.one must not / we must not
l'uniforme scolaire (m)school uniform
porterto wear
se leverto get up
je me lèveI get up
il y a / il n'y a pas dethere is/are / there is/are no
la récréationbreak time
les cours commencentlessons start

Grammar focus: school rules. Use il est interdit de + infinitive for things that are banned: Il est interdit de courir dans les couloirs (It is forbidden to run in the corridors). Use on doit + infinitive for obligations: On doit porter l'uniforme scolaire (We must wear school uniform). Use on ne doit pas + infinitive for prohibitions: On ne doit pas utiliser son portable en classe (We must not use our phone in class).

Reflexive verbs need a reflexive pronoun (me, te, se, nous, vous, se) before the verb: je me lève à sept heures (I get up at seven o'clock). In the negative: je ne me lève pas tôt (I don't get up early).

Model paragraph: Dans mon école il y a une grande bibliothèque et un terrain de sport. On doit porter l'uniforme scolaire. Il est interdit d'utiliser son portable en classe. Je me lève à sept heures pour arriver à l'heure. (In my school there is a large library and a sports field. We must wear school uniform. It is forbidden to use your phone in class. I get up at seven o'clock to arrive on time.)

method_card.title: Jobs, Work Experience and Future Plans
method_card.content:
This lesson covers jobs and professions, work experience (le stage en entreprise), and ways to talk about future plans. You need three key structures: je voudrais / j'aimerais + infinitif for wishes, the futur simple for what you will do, and opinion phrases like c'est bien payé or c'est stressant.

FrançaisEnglish
le métier / la professionjob / profession
le médecindoctor
l'infirmier / l'infirmièrenurse (m/f)
l'avocat(e)lawyer
l'ingénieur(e)engineer
le/la comptableaccountant
le/la journalistejournalist
le/la professeur(e)teacher
le stage en entreprisework experience
travaillerto work
bien payé(e)well paid
stressant(e)stressful
passionnant(e)exciting / fascinating
je travailleraiI will work
j'aimerais devenirI would like to become

Grammar focus: the future tense (futur simple). For most verbs, add the endings -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont to the infinitive (removing the final -e for -re verbs). Examples: je travaillerai (I will work), j'habiterai (I will live), je finirai (I will finish). Some common verbs are irregular: être → je serai, avoir → j'aurai, aller → j'irai, faire → je ferai, pouvoir → je pourrai, vouloir → je voudrai.

Model paragraph: En ce moment, je voudrais devenir médecin parce que c'est un métier passionnant et bien payé. lessons.title: Holidays and Travel Plans
lessons.description: Talk about holidays and travel plans using the preterite, present, and conditional tenses.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for holidays, travel and destinations
Master ir a + infinitive to express travel plans
Use the future tense endings to say what you will do on holiday
Contrast present habits with future plans using normalmente and el verano que viene
method_card.title: Holidays and Travel Plans
method_card.content:
This lesson covers holiday vocabulary, travel destinations, types of holiday and how to talk about future travel plans. Two key grammar structures are central: ir a + infinitive (going to do something) and the simple future tense (will do something) — both essential for discussing plans.

SpanishEnglish
las vacacionesholidays / vacation
el destinodestination
el vueloflight
el alojamientoaccommodation
la playabeach
la montañamountain
el extranjeroabroad / foreign country
el crucerocruise
el campingcampsite / camping
viajarto travel
alojarseto stay (accommodation)
ir de vacacionesto go on holiday
tomar el solto sunbathe
el verano que vienenext summer
normalmente / suelo irusually / I usually go

Grammar focus: future plans with ir a + infinitive and the future tense. Use ir a + infinitive for immediate or decided plans: Voy a viajar a Francia (I am going to travel to France). Use the future tense for more distant or uncertain plans: Iré a la playa (I will go to the beach). Form the future by adding endings to the infinitive: -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án. Contrast with the present tense to describe habits: Normalmente voy a España, pero este año iré a Italia (I usually go to Spain, but this year I will go to Italy).

Model paragraph: Normalmente voy de vacaciones a España con mi familia porque me encanta la playa. El verano que viene, voy a viajar a Francia en avión y me alojaré en un hotel de lujo. (I usually go on holiday to Spain with my family because I love the beach. Next summer, I am going to travel to France by plane and I will stay in a luxury hotel.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — holidays and travel appear across listening, speaking, reading and writing every year

lessons.title: Accommodation and Hotels
lessons.description: Book hotels, describe accommodation, and deal with problems using key phrases.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for accommodation types and hotel facilities
Use quisiera / me gustaría to make polite booking requests
Practise asking about facilities with ¿Tiene…?
Describe problems using hay + problem or no funciona + item
method_card.title: Accommodation and Hotels
method_card.content:
This lesson covers accommodation types, hotel vocabulary, and the language you need to make bookings and requests. In a hotel or hostel you will need to ask for rooms, describe problems, and use polite register with quisiera or me gustaría.

SpanishEnglish
el hotelthe hotel
el albergue (juvenil)the (youth) hostel
el campingthe campsite
la pensiónthe guesthouse / B&B
una habitación individuala single room
una habitación doblea double room
con ducha / con bañowith shower / with bathroom
la recepciónthe reception
el ascensorthe lift
el aparcamientothe car park
media pensiónhalf board
pensión completafull board
quisiera reservarI would like to book
¿tiene…?do you have…?
el aire acondicionadothe air conditioning

Grammar focus: quisiera and the conditional for polite requests. Quisiera (I would like) is the imperfect subjunctive of querer used as a polite formula — treat it as a fixed phrase. Me gustaría (conditional of gustar) works the same way. Both are far more polite than quiero (I want). For complaints use hay + problem: Hay demasiado ruido (There is too much noise); no funciona el aire acondicionado (the air conditioning is not working).

Model paragraph: Quisiera reservar una habitación doble con baño para tres noches. ¿Tiene habitaciones con vistas al mar? Lamentablemente hay un problema — no funciona la ducha. (I would like to book a double room with bathroom for three nights. Do you have rooms with sea views? Unfortunately there is a problem — the shower is not working.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — accommodation and travel appear across speaking, listening, reading and writing every year

gold.source_text: Last summer we stayed in a campsite near the beach. Although it was cheap, the facilities were not very clean and there was a lot of noise.

Accept any grammatically correct translation that conveys the same meaning. Check: correct preterite vs imperfect (stayed = preterite; era/había = imperfect for description/background), adjective agreement (limpias agrees with instalaciones, feminine plural), aunque + imperfect. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

gaps.correct_explain: reservara (or reservase) is the imperfect subjunctive of reservar. After si in a past hypothetical or indirect speech context, Spanish requires the imperfect subjunctive.

lessons.title: Transport and Directions
lessons.description: Learn transport vocabulary, ask for and give directions, and use prepositions of place.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for means of transport and direction phrases
Use en + vehicle (or a pie) to say how you travel
Give directions using imperative verbs: sigue, gira, cruza
Locate places using estar + preposition of place (al lado de, enfrente de, etc.)
method_card.title: Transport and Directions
method_card.content:
This lesson covers means of transport, buying tickets, and asking for or giving directions. Two key structures underpin everything: using en + vehicle for transport modes, and direction verbs such as sigue, gira and cruza for giving instructions.

SpanishEnglish
en cocheby car
en autobúsby bus
en trenby train
en metroby underground / metro
en aviónby plane
a pieon foot
coger / tomar el trento take the train
sigue todo rectogo straight on
gira a la derechaturn right
gira a la izquierdaturn left
cruza el puentecross the bridge
está al lado deit is next to
está enfrente deit is opposite
un billete de idaa single ticket
un billete de ida y vueltaa return ticket

Grammar focus: prepositions of place and imperative verbs for directions. Use estar for location: La estación está al lado del banco (The station is next to the bank). Direction commands use the imperative (tú form): sigue, gira, cruza, toma. Note the preposition contraction: al = a + el (never a el). For transport use en + vehicle but a pie (on foot — no en).

Model paragraph: Normalmente voy al instituto en autobús, pero los fines de semana cojo el tren para visitar a mis amigos. Para llegar a la estación, sigue todo recto y luego gira a la derecha; está enfrente del supermercado. (I usually go to school by bus, but at weekends I take the train to visit my friends. To get to the station, go straight on and then turn right; it is opposite the supermarket.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — transport and directions appear across listening, reading, speaking and writing every year

gold.source_text: Yesterday I took the train to Madrid, but usually I travel by car because it is faster. If I had more money, I would always buy a return ticket.
model_answers: Ayer cogí el tren a Madrid, pero normalmente viajo en coche porque es más rápido. Si tuviera más dinero, siempre compraría un billete de ida y vuelta.

Accept any grammatically correct translation that conveys the same meaning. Check: preterite (cogí), present (viajo), comparatives (más rápido), conditional (compraría), and imperfect subjunctive (tuviera) or acceptable conditional alternatives. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

gaps.rule: Imperfect subjunctive in si-clause (conditional sentence type 2)

wrong.tengo: tengo is the present indicative. Hypothetical si-clauses (if I had…) need the imperfect subjunctive → tuviera.
wrong.tendría: tendría is the conditional (I would have). The si-clause takes the imperfect subjunctive; the main clause takes the conditional → tuviera … iría.

gaps.correct_explain: tuviera is the imperfect subjunctive of tener. In a hypothetical si-clause (if I had…) you always use the imperfect subjunctive, never the present or conditional.

gaps.rule: Conditional in the main clause (type 2 conditional sentence)

wrong.fui: fui is the preterite (I went). The main clause needs the conditional → iría.
wrong.voy: voy is the present indicative. The main clause of a hypothetical sentence uses the conditional → iría.

gaps.correct_explain: iría is the conditional of ir. After an imperfect subjunctive si-clause, the main clause uses the conditional.

wrong.por: por does not express means of transport. Use en for vehicles.

wrong.va: va is the él/ella form. You need the first person → voy.
wrong.vamos: vamos is the nosotros form (we go). The subject here is yo → voy.

gaps.correct_explain: voy is the yo form of ir (to go) in the present tense.

gaps.correct_explain: comprar (to buy) is the infinitive. After quisiera you always use the infinitive.

gaps.rule: Fixed phrase — billete de ida y vuelta

wrong.o: o means 'or' and breaks the fixed phrase. A return ticket is always de ida y vuelta.
wrong.de: de would give de ida de vuelta — not standard Spanish. The fixed phrase needs y.

gaps.correct_explain: y (and) is part of the fixed phrase de ida y vuelta (return/round trip).

lessons.title: Weather and Holiday Activities
lessons.description: Describe weather and holiday activities using the preterite and past continuous tenses.

steps: Learn the key weather expressions using hace, hay and llueve/nieva
Link weather to activities with cuando + present tense
Use the preterite and imperfect to describe past holidays and weather conditions
Use the future and conditional to talk about planned or hypothetical holiday activities
method_card.title: Weather and Holiday Activities
method_card.content:
This lesson covers the weather in Spanish, the seasons, and how to link weather to holiday activities — including what you did in different conditions and what you would do in the future.

SpanishEnglish
hace solit is sunny
hace calorit is hot
hace fríoit is cold
hace vientoit is windy
llueve / está lloviendoit rains / it is raining
nieva / está nevandoit snows / it is snowing
hay tormentathere is a storm
hay nieblathere is fog
la primavera / el veranospring / summer
el otoño / el inviernoautumn / winter
ir a la playato go to the beach
hacer senderismoto go hiking
quedarse en casato stay at home
cuando hace solwhen it is sunny
si hiciera solif it were sunny (conditional trigger)

Grammar focus: linking weather to activities across tenses. Use cuando + present tense to describe habits: Cuando hace sol, voy a la playa. Use preterite for completed past actions and imperfect for background conditions: Cuando hacía mal tiempo, nos quedábamos en el hotel. For future plans use the immediate future (voy a…) or simple future (iré…); for hypothetical plans use the conditional: Si hiciera sol, iría a la playa.

Model paragraph: Cuando hace sol me encanta ir a la playa con mi familia. El verano pasado fuimos a la costa — hacía mucho calor y nadamos en el mar todos los días. Si hiciera buen tiempo el año que viene, iría de nuevo a España. (When it is sunny I love going to the beach with my family. Last summer we went to the coast — it was very hot and we swam in the sea every day. If the weather were good next year, I would go to Spain again.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — weather and holiday activities appear across speaking, listening, reading and writing every year

gold.source_text: When the weather was good, we used to go to the beach, but when it was raining we would visit the local museums and monuments.
model_answers: Cuando hacía buen tiempo, íbamos a la playa, pero cuando llovía visitábamos los museos y monumentos del lugar.

Accept any grammatically correct translation that conveys the same meaning. Check: correct use of imperfect throughout for habitual past (hacía, íbamos, llovía, visitábamos), appropriate connectives, word order. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

distractor_labels.haría: wrong form for weather — si + imperfect subjunctive triggers conditional: hiciera calor (not haría calor)

wrong.hace: hace is present indicative — used for real/likely conditions. For hypothetical 'if' use the imperfect subjunctive → hiciera.
wrong.hará: hará is future tense. Hypothetical si-clauses never take the future — use imperfect subjunctive → hiciera.

gaps.correct_explain: Hiciera is the imperfect subjunctive of hacer. In a hypothetical conditional, the si-clause uses the imperfect subjunctive.

gaps.rule: Conditional tense in the main clause

wrong.voy: voy is present tense. You need the conditional → iría.
wrong.iré: iré is the future (I will go) — used after real conditions. Hypothetical si + imperfect subjunctive → conditional in the main clause.

gaps.correct_explain: Iría is the conditional of ir (I would go) — the main clause after a hypothetical si-clause uses the conditional.

wrong.tomo: tomo is present tense (I sunbathe). The hypothetical conditional requires tomaría.
wrong.tomé: tomé is preterite (I sunbathed). The hypothetical conditional requires tomaría.

gaps.correct_explain: Tomaría is the conditional of tomar (I would sunbathe/take). Regular -ar verbs add -ía to the infinitive.

wrong.es: es is not used for weather in this way in Spanish. Use hace for temperature/sun/wind.
wrong.hay: hay is used for hay tormenta / hay niebla — but sunny/hot/cold weather uses hace.

gaps.correct_explain: hace is the correct third-person singular of hacer used for weather expressions like hace sol, hace calor.

wrong.fui: fui is preterite (I went). After me gusta use the infinitive → ir.
wrong.voy: voy is a conjugated verb. After me gusta use the infinitive → ir.

gaps.correct_explain: After me gusta you always use the infinitive: me gusta ir.

gaps.correct_explain: hacía is the imperfect of hacer, used for ongoing background conditions in the past.

wrong.nadaron: nadaron is third-person plural (they swam). The subject is implied nosotros → nadamos.
wrong.nadábamos: nadábamos is imperfect and implies a habitual background activity. Here the swimming is a completed holiday action → preterite nadamos.

gaps.correct_explain: nadamos is the nosotros preterite of nadar — a completed repeated action in the past.

gaps.correct_explain: veíamos is the nosotros imperfect of ver — habitual past activity.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Hacía (imperfect) describes ongoing background conditions: Hacía mucho calor — it was very hot (setting the scene).

steps.label: Step 2

lessons.title: Technology and Social Media
lessons.description: Discuss technology use, social media advantages and disadvantages, and screen time.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for digital devices and their uses
Master the para + infinitive structure to express purpose
Practice giving balanced opinions on the advantages and disadvantages of technology
Use a range of verbs (usar, navegar, descargar) to describe how you use different devices
method_card.title: Technology and Social Media
method_card.content:
This lesson covers digital devices and how we use technology in everyday life. The key structure is usar + noun (to use a device) and para + infinitive (in order to / for doing something): Uso mi móvil para escuchar música (I use my phone to listen to music).

SpanishEnglish
el móvilmobile phone
el ordenador (portátil)(laptop) computer
la tablettablet
los videojuegosvideo games
los auricularesheadphones
la pantallascreen
descargarto download
navegar por internetto browse the internet
mandar mensajesto send messages
hacer videollamadasto make video calls
las ventajasthe advantages
los inconvenientesthe disadvantages
imprescindibleessential / indispensable
adicto/a aaddicted to
la bateríabattery

Grammar focus: para + infinitive. Use para followed by an infinitive to express purpose (in order to / for). The infinitive never changes: Uso el ordenador para hacer los deberes (I use the computer to do my homework). This works after any verb or noun: un móvil para llamar (a phone for calling).

Model paragraph: Uso mi móvil para escuchar música y para mandar mensajes a mis amigos. Creo que la tecnología es muy útil, pero puede ser adictiva. (I use my phone to listen to music and to send messages to my friends. I think technology is very useful, but it can be addictive.)

model_answers: Aunque la tecnología tiene muchas ventajas, algunos jóvenes pasan demasiado tiempo con el móvil y puede afectar su sueño.

gaps.rule: Present subjunctive — querer que + subjunctive (yo form of pasar)

wrong.paso: paso is the present indicative (I spend). After querer que, Spanish requires the subjunctive → pase.

wrong.sale: sale is the él/ella indicative. The subjunctive yo form of salir is salga.
wrong.salgo: salgo is the present indicative (I go out). After querer que, use the subjunctive → salga.

gaps.correct_explain: salga is the irregular present subjunctive of salir (yo). The go-verb salgo forms the subjunctive stem: salg- + -a.

method_card.title: My House and Home
method_card.content:
This lesson covers the rooms of a house, furniture, and how to describe your home. Use hay (there is/there are) to say what is in a room, and prepositions of place to describe exactly where things are.

SpanishEnglish
la cocinakitchen
el dormitoriobedroom
el salónliving room
el cuarto de bañobathroom
el comedordining room
el jardíngarden
la camabed
el sofásofa
la mesatable
la sillachair
al lado denext to
encima deon top of / above
debajo deunder / below
haythere is / there are
el armariowardrobe

Grammar focus: hay + prepositions of place. Hay never changes — use it for both singular and plural: Hay una cama (there is a bed), Hay dos sillas (there are two chairs). Combine hay with a preposition of place to say exactly where something is: El libro está encima de la mesa (The book is on the table). Note: for the location of a specific item, use estar, not ser.

To contract: a + el = al — so al lado del sofá (next to the sofa). De + el = del — debajo del armario (under the wardrobe).

Model paragraph: En mi casa hay seis habitaciones. Mi dormitorio es pequeño pero acogedor. Hay una cama al lado de la ventana y el armario está debajo de las escaleras. Normalmente hago mis deberes en mi dormitorio. (In my house there are six rooms. My bedroom is small but cosy. There is a bed next to the window and the wardrobe is under the stairs. I usually do my homework in my bedroom.)

method_card.title: My Town and Local Area
method_card.content:
This lesson covers vocabulary for places in a town, describing where you live and giving opinions about your local area. Two key grammar structures are central: hay / no hay (there is/are / there is not/are not) for describing what a place has to offer, and comparisons using más ... que (more ... than) and menos ... que (less ... than).

SpanishEnglish
el ayuntamientotown hall
el polideportivosports centre
el cinecinema
las tiendasshops
el mercadomarket
la bibliotecalibrary
el parquepark
la plaza mayormain square
el barrioneighbourhood / district
el pueblovillage / small town
la ciudadcity
tranquilo/aquiet / peaceful
animado/alively
haythere is / there are
no haythere is not / there are not

Grammar focus: hay / no hay and comparisons. Use hay (never changes) to say what exists: Hay un cine y un polideportivo (There is a cinema and a sports centre). Use no hay for what is missing: No hay teatro (There is no theatre). For comparisons, use más + adjective + que: Mi pueblo es más tranquilo que la ciudad (My village is quieter than the city). Use menos + adjective + que: El barrio es menos animado que el centro (The neighbourhood is less lively than the centre).

Model paragraph: Vivo en un pueblo pequeño en el norte de España. Hay un parque y unas tiendas, pero no hay cine ni polideportivo. Mi pueblo es más tranquilo que la ciudad, aunque a veces es un poco aburrido. (I live in a small village in the north of Spain. There is a park and some shops, but there is no cinema or sports centre. My village is quieter than the city, although sometimes it is a bit boring.)

lessons.title: The Environment and Global Issues
lessons.description: Discuss environmental problems, recycling, and what we should do using the future tense.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for environmental problems and global issues
Use hay que and se debe + infinitive to express what should be done
Use deberíamos + infinitive to give opinions about environmental action
Use es necesario que + subjunctive for Higher-level obligation structures
method_card.title: The Environment and Global Issues
method_card.content:
This lesson covers environmental problems and what we can do to protect the planet — a key topic in speaking and writing tasks. You will need vocabulary for environmental issues (la contaminación, el cambio climático, la basura) and structures for expressing obligation: hay que, se debe, and deberíamos.

SpanishEnglish
el medio ambientethe environment
la contaminaciónpollution
el cambio climáticoclimate change
la basurarubbish / waste
el calentamiento globalglobal warming
la deforestacióndeforestation
reciclarto recycle
ahorrar energíato save energy
proteger el planetato protect the planet
hay queone must / we need to
se debeone should / it is necessary to
deberíamoswe should (conditional)
el transporte públicopublic transport
renovablerenewable
sosteniblesustainable

Grammar focus: expressing obligation — hay que, se debe, deberíamos. All three express what should be done. Hay que + infinitive is impersonal: Hay que reciclar más (We need to recycle more). Se debe + infinitive is formal: Se debe ahorrar energía (One should save energy). Deberíamos + infinitive is the conditional of deber (we should): Deberíamos usar el transporte público (We should use public transport).

For Higher tier: use the present subjunctive after impersonal expressions of necessity: Es necesario que reciclemos (It is necessary that we recycle). Trigger phrase: es necesario que / es importante que / es urgente que → subjunctive.

Model paragraph: El cambio climático es un problema global muy grave. Hay que reciclar la basura y ahorrar energía en casa. En mi opinión, deberíamos usar más el transporte público para reducir la contaminación. (Climate change is a very serious global problem. We need to recycle waste and save energy at home. In my opinion, we should use public transport more to reduce pollution.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — the environment appears across speaking, listening, reading and writing every year

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for free-time activities and hobbies

method_card.title: Free-Time Activities and Hobbies
method_card.content:
This lesson covers free-time activities and hobbies. Use j'aime / j'adore / je préfère followed by an infinitive to express what you like or love doing. The key verbs for activities are jouer (to play), faire (to do/play), sortir (to go out) and lire (to read).

FrançaisEnglish
jouer au footto play football
jouer aux jeux vidéoto play video games
faire du sportto do sport
faire du véloto go cycling
faire de la natationto go swimming
lire un livreto read a book
écouter de la musiqueto listen to music
regarder des filmsto watch films
sortir avec des amisto go out with friends
dessiner / peindreto draw / to paint
souventoften
tous les joursevery day
le week-endat the weekend
de temps en tempsfrom time to time
j'adore / j'aime / je n'aime pasI love / I like / I don't like

Grammar focus: j'aime + infinitive. In French, after verbs of liking (aimer, adorer, préférer, détester), use the infinitive of the following verb: j'adore jouer au foot (I love playing football). Note that jouer au/aux is used for sports played with a ball or opponent, while faire du/de la/de l' is used for other sports and activities. Jouer au foot, jouer aux cartes — faire du vélo, faire de la natation.

Model paragraph: Le week-end, j'aime faire du sport avec mes amis. J'adore jouer au foot et je fais souvent de la natation. Le soir, je préfère regarder des films ou lire un bon livre. (At the weekend, I like doing sport with my friends. I love playing football and I often go swimming. In the evening, I prefer watching films or reading a good book.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — free-time activities appear across speaking, listening, reading and writing every year

method_card.title: Music, Film and Television
method_card.content:
This lesson covers vocabulary for music, film and television. You will express opinions and preferences using key phrases, describe something you watched using the perfect tense, and compare things using comparatives.

FrançaisEnglish
la musiquemusic
un filma film
une émissiona (TV) programme
une sériea (TV) series
un dessin animéa cartoon
le rap / le jazz / la poprap / jazz / pop (music)
écouterto listen (to)
regarderto watch
je préfèreI prefer
ce que j'aime c'estwhat I like is
j'ai regardéI watched (perfect tense)
j'ai écoutéI listened (perfect tense)
passionnant(e)gripping / exciting
ennuyeux / ennuyeuseboring (m/f)
plus… quemore… than

Grammar focus: the perfect tense (le passé composé). To say what you watched or listened to in the past, use avoir + past participle: J'ai regardé (I watched), J'ai écouté (I listened). Regular -er verbs drop -er and add -é: regarder → regardé, écouter → écouté. The past participle does not change for gender/number when the auxiliary is avoir.

Comparatives: plus + adjective + que (more … than), moins + adjective + que (less … than), aussi + adjective + que (as … as). Example: Les films d'action sont plus passionnants que les comédies. (Action films are more gripping than comedies.)

Model paragraph: Ce que j'aime c'est écouter de la musique pop. Hier soir j'ai regardé un film d'horreur à la télé. Il était plus intéressant que la série que j'ai regardée la semaine dernière. (What I like is listening to pop music. Last night I watched a horror film on TV. It was more interesting than the series I watched last week.)

method_card.title: Sport and Sporting Events
method_card.content:
This lesson covers sports, sporting events and talking about watching or attending them. There are two key structures for saying which sport you do: use faire du / de la / de l' for individual sports and activities, and jouer au / à la / à l' for ball and team games.

FrançaisEnglish
le sportsport
un matcha match / game
un tournoia tournament
un stadea stadium
une équipea team
jouer au footballto play football
jouer au tennisto play tennis
faire du véloto cycle / go cycling
faire de la natationto swim / go swimming
faire de l'athlétismeto do athletics
regarder un matchto watch a match
assister à un événementto attend an event

Grammar focus: faire du/de la vs jouer au/à la. For individual sports and activities use faire de + the definite article, which contracts: faire du vélo, faire de la natation, faire de l'athlétisme. For ball and team games use jouer à + the definite article: jouer au football (au = à + le), jouer à la pétanque, jouer aux échecs. Never mix the two — do not say faire du football or jouer à la natation.

Perfect tense for past events: Use the passé composé to say what you watched or did. Most verbs take avoir: j'ai regardé le match (I watched the match), j'ai joué au tennis (I played tennis). Some verbs of movement take être: je suis allé(e) au stade (I went to the stadium).

Model paragraph: Le week-end dernier, j'ai regardé un match de football à la télévision. Mon équipe préférée a gagné et c'était vraiment passionnant. En général, je joue au tennis deux fois par semaine. (Last weekend, I watched a football match on television. My favourite team won and it was really exciting. In general, I play tennis twice a week.)

lessons.title: French Festivals and Celebrations
lessons.description: French festivals including Noël, Pâques, la fête nationale, Carnaval and Aïd with celebration vocabulary.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for French-speaking festivals and celebrations
Use the perfect tense (passé composé) with avoir to describe past celebrations
Apply the correct past participle and auxiliary verb for each activity
Build extended sentences describing what you did and your opinions using connectives
method_card.title: French Festivals and Celebrations
method_card.content:
This lesson covers major festivals and celebrations in the French-speaking world. To talk about past celebrations, you use the passé composé (perfect tense): avoir or être + past participle. Most verbs use avoir: j'ai célébré (I celebrated), nous avons regardé (we watched).

FrançaisEnglish
la fête / la célébrationthe festival / the celebration
le 14 juillet / la Fête nationaleBastille Day / National Day
le feu d'artificethe fireworks display
le défilé militairethe military parade
NoëlChristmas
le Nouvel An / la Saint-SylvestreNew Year / New Year's Eve
la Fête de la Musiquethe Music Festival (21 June)
Mardi GrasMardi Gras (Fat Tuesday)
le carnavalthe carnival
les costumes (m)the costumes
la bûche de Noëlthe Christmas log cake
les cadeaux (m)the gifts / presents
célébrer / fêterto celebrate
j'ai assisté àI attended
nous avons regardéwe watched

Grammar focus: the perfect tense (passé composé) with avoir. To say what you did, use the present tense of avoir + the past participle. For -er verbs, remove -er and add -é: célébrer → célébré, regarder → regardé, manger → mangé. Example: J'ai célébré le 14 juillet avec ma famille. (I celebrated Bastille Day with my family.) For negative: Je n'ai pas regardé le défilé. (I didn't watch the parade.)

Model paragraph: L'année dernière, j'ai célébré le 14 juillet avec ma famille. Nous avons regardé le feu d'artifice et nous avons mangé ensemble. C'était magnifique et très animé. (Last year, I celebrated Bastille Day with my family. We watched the fireworks and we ate together. It was magnificent and very lively.)

lessons.title: Customs and How We Celebrate
lessons.description: Describing past and future celebrations, cultural traditions, weddings and direct object pronouns.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for celebrations and customs
Use the imperfect tense (quand j'étais petit, on célébrait) for habitual past actions
Use d'habitude + present tense for current regular habits
Build extended sentences with time phrases and connectives such as chaque année and d'abord
method_card.title: Customs and How We Celebrate
method_card.content:
This lesson covers family celebrations and customs — birthdays, weddings, Christmas and New Year's Eve — including traditional food and how to describe habitual past events using the imperfect tense.

FrenchEnglish
l'anniversaire (m)birthday
le mariagewedding
Noël (m)Christmas
le réveillonChristmas Eve / New Year's Eve celebration
fêterto celebrate
la coutumecustom / tradition
la fêtecelebration / party
offrir des cadeauxto give gifts
la bûche de NoëlChristmas log cake
le sapin de NoëlChristmas tree
se réunir en familleto get together as a family
d'habitudeusually / as a rule
quand j'étais petit(e)when I was little
on célébraitwe used to celebrate
les décorations (f)decorations

Grammar focus: the imperfect tense for habitual past actions. Use the imperfect (l'imparfait) to describe what you used to do as a child or what always happened. Form it by taking the nous present stem and adding: -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient. For example: célébrer → nous célébrons → célébr-, so on célébrait (we used to celebrate). Trigger phrases include quand j'étais petit(e), chaque année (every year), and d'habitude (usually). The present tense + d'habitude describes current habits.

Model paragraph: Quand j'étais petit, on célébrait Noël en famille. D'habitude, on se retrouvait chez mes grands-parents et on mangeait la bûche de Noël ensemble. (When I was little, we used to celebrate Christmas as a family. Usually, we would meet at my grandparents' house and eat the Christmas log cake together.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — celebrations and customs appear in reading, listening, speaking and writing tasks

lessons.title: Celebrity Culture and Role Models
lessons.description: Describing celebrities and role models using demonstrative adjectives and the imperative mood.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for celebrities and role models (les célébrités et les modèles)
Use qui (who/which) for subject relative clauses and que (whom/which) for object relative clauses
Express admiration using j'admire, je trouve que and c'est quelqu'un qui…
Build extended opinions with parce que, car and grâce à to explain why someone inspires you
method_card.title: Celebrity Culture and Role Models
method_card.content:
This lesson covers celebrities, role models and the language of admiration. The key grammar focus is relative pronouns: use qui when the relative clause's verb has no separate subject, and que (qu' before a vowel) when there is already a subject in the clause.

FrançaisEnglish
une célébritéa celebrity
un modèle / un exemple à suivrea role model
une personne que j'admirea person I admire
inspirerto inspire
influencerto influence
le couragecourage
la déterminationdetermination
la générositégenerosity
talentueux / talentueusetalented
courageux / courageusecourageous, brave
ambitieux / ambitieuseambitious
généreux / généreusegenerous
admirerto admire
grâce àthanks to
je trouve queI find that / I think that

Grammar focus: relative pronouns qui and que. Qui replaces a subject: C'est une personne qui m'inspire beaucoup (She is a person who inspires me a lot — qui is the subject of inspire). Que replaces an object: C'est une personne que j'admire (She is a person whom I admire — j' is the subject, que is the object). Before a vowel or silent h, que becomes qu': un artiste qu'on admire.

Model paragraph: Mon modèle est une sportive que j'admire depuis longtemps. C'est quelqu'un qui travaille très dur et qui ne se décourage jamais. Grâce à sa détermination, elle est devenue championne du monde. Je la trouve vraiment courageuse et ambitieuse. (My role model is a sportswoman I have admired for a long time. She is someone who works very hard and never gives up. Thanks to her determination, she became world champion. I find her truly courageous and ambitious.)

exam_context.frequency: Common topic in writing and speaking — expressing admiration and explaining who inspires you

gold.source_text: The celebrity I admire the most is a scientist who has dedicated her life to helping others. Thanks to her determination and generosity, she has changed the lives of thousands of people.

gaps.rule: Present subjunctive of être after bien que

wrong.est: est is the indicative (normal) present tense. After bien que, you must use the subjunctive → soit.

wrong.humblée: humblée does not exist as an adjective form in French.

gaps.correct_explain: humble — adjectives ending in -e in the masculine do not change for the feminine. Une personne humble is correct for both genders.

lessons.title: Social Media and Online Life
lessons.description: Social media vocabulary, discussing advantages and disadvantages of online life with relative pronouns.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for social media and online activities
Use pour + infinitif to explain why you use the internet
Give balanced opinions using avantages/inconvénients with connectives
Practise the subjunctive after je ne pense pas que for Higher tasks
method_card.title: Social Media and Online Life
method_card.content:
This lesson covers social media, online activities and how to discuss the advantages and disadvantages of life on the internet. You will also practise giving opinions and using pour + infinitif to express purpose.

FrançaisEnglish
les réseaux sociauxsocial networks / social media
publier des photosto post photos
tchatter en ligneto chat online
naviguer sur internetto browse the internet
télécharger de la musiqueto download music
partager des vidéosto share videos
les avantagesthe advantages
les inconvénientsthe disadvantages
la sécurité en ligneonline safety
le cyberharcèlementcyberbullying
rester en contactto stay in contact
dépendre de son téléphoneto depend on one's phone
à mon avisin my opinion
selon moiaccording to me / in my view
je ne pense pas que…I don't think that… (+ subjunctive)

Grammar focus: pour + infinitif. Use pour followed by an infinitive to express purpose (in order to): J'utilise les réseaux sociaux pour rester en contact avec mes amis. (I use social media to stay in contact with my friends.) The verb after pour is always the infinitive — never conjugated.

Model paragraph: À mon avis, les réseaux sociaux ont beaucoup d'avantages. J'utilise internet pour tchatter avec mes amis et pour partager des photos. Cependant, je ne pense pas que ce soit toujours sûr. (In my opinion, social media has many advantages. I use the internet to chat with my friends and to share photos. However, I don't think it is always safe.)

lessons.title: Eating Out and Restaurant Conversations
lessons.description: Restaurant vocabulary, ordering food and drink in a role-play scenario with partitive articles.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for restaurants, menus and dishes (la carte, les plats)
Use je voudrais / je vais prendre / pour moi to order politely
Use the perfect tense (passé composé) to say what you ate
Use the imperfect (imparfait) to describe the meal — c'était délicieux, c'était trop salé
method_card.title: Eating Out and Restaurant Conversations
method_card.content:
This lesson covers eating out at a French restaurant or café, including reading the menu, ordering politely and giving opinions on the meal. Two tenses are key: the passé composé for what you ate (j'ai mangé), and the imparfait for descriptions (c'était délicieux).

FrançaisEnglish
le restaurant / le caférestaurant / café
la carte / le menuthe menu (à la carte / set menu)
les platsthe dishes / courses
l'entrée (f)starter
le plat principalmain course
le dessertdessert
je voudrais / je vais prendreI would like / I'm going to have
pour moi, ...for me, ...
l'addition (f)the bill
le pourboirethe tip
délicieux / délicieusedelicious
savoureux / savoureusetasty
trop salé(e) / trop sucré(e)too salty / too sweet
le serveur / la serveusewaiter / waitress
réserver une tableto book a table

Grammar focus: ordering and describing. To order politely, use the conditional: je voudrais (I would like) or the near future: je vais prendre (I'm going to have). For opinions on the meal, use c'était (it was — imparfait of être) for descriptions: C'était délicieux ! For saying what you ordered, use the passé composé: j'ai commandé, j'ai mangé, j'ai pris.

Model paragraph: Hier soir, nous sommes allés au restaurant. J'ai commandé une salade comme entrée et un steak comme plat principal. C'était vraiment délicieux et le service était excellent. À la fin, nous avons demandé l'addition. (Last night, we went to the restaurant. I ordered a salad as a starter and a steak as a main course. It was really delicious and the service was excellent. At the end, we asked for the bill.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — eating out appears in reading, listening, speaking and writing across all papers

lessons.title: Holidays and Travel Plans
lessons.description: Key holiday vocabulary, countries, transport and the near future tense with aller + infinitive.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for holidays, destinations and types of travel
Use aller + infinitive (je vais voyager) to express near future plans
Use the simple future tense (j'irai, nous irons) for more distant or certain plans
Give opinions and preferences about holidays using j'aime, je préfère, je trouve que
method_card.title: Holidays and Travel Plans
method_card.content:
This lesson covers holiday vocabulary, types of holiday and how to talk about travel plans. Two tenses are essential: the near future (aller + infinitif) for 'going to do' and the simple future for 'will do'.

FrançaisEnglish
les vacances (f pl)the holidays
la destinationthe destination
l'étranger (m)abroad / foreign country
la plagethe beach
la montagnethe mountains
la campagnethe countryside
l'hôtel (m)the hotel
le campingcamping / campsite
le volthe flight
le trainthe train
voyagerto travel
bronzer / se bronzerto sunbathe
visiterto visit (a place)
se reposerto relax / to rest
l'an prochain / l'été prochainnext year / next summer

Grammar focus: near future vs simple future. Use aller + infinitif for plans you are going to do soon: Je vais voyager en Espagne cet été. (I am going to travel to Spain this summer.) Use the simple future for plans further ahead or to sound more confident: J'irai en France l'an prochain. (I will go to France next year.) Key future stems: aller → ir-, avoir → aur-, être → ser-, faire → fer-, venir → viendr-. Future endings: -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont.

Model paragraph: D'habitude, je pars en vacances en France avec ma famille. Nous restons dans un hôtel près de la plage. L'année prochaine, j'irai à l'étranger — je vais visiter le Portugal parce que j'adore la mer et le soleil. (Usually, I go on holiday in France with my family. We stay in a hotel near the beach. Next year, I will go abroad — I am going to visit Portugal because I love the sea and the sun.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — holidays and travel appear across listening, speaking, reading and writing every year

method_card.title: Past Holidays and Experiences
method_card.content:
This lesson covers how to talk about past holidays and experiences in French. You need two past tenses working together: the passé composé for completed actions, and the imparfait for descriptions and ongoing states.

FrançaisEnglish
les vacances (f. pl.)the holidays
la plagethe beach
la montagnethe mountain(s)
l'étranger (m.)abroad
l'hôtel (m.)the hotel
le campingthe campsite
aller à / ento go to
visiterto visit
se baignerto swim / bathe
bronzerto sunbathe
faire du véloto go cycling
il faisait beauthe weather was nice
il faisait chaudit was hot
c'était magnifiqueit was magnificent
c'était nulit was rubbish

Grammar focus: passé composé with être. Most verbs use avoir as the auxiliary: j'ai visité (I visited), j'ai mangé (I ate). However, a group of verbs — mainly verbs of movement and reflexive verbs — use être: je suis allé(e) (I went), je suis parti(e) (I left). With être verbs, the past participle must agree with the subject: add -e for feminine, -s for masculine plural, -es for feminine plural.

Use the imperfect for descriptions and weather: il faisait beau (the weather was nice), c'était super (it was great), il y avait beaucoup de touristes (there were lots of tourists).

Model paragraph: L'année dernière, je suis allée en Espagne avec ma famille. Nous avons visité Barcelone et nous nous sommes baignés dans la mer. Il faisait très chaud et c'était magnifique. (Last year, I went to Spain with my family. We visited Barcelona and we swam in the sea. It was very hot and it was magnificent.) [Written by a female speaker — note allée with the extra -e.]

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — past holidays and experiences appear in speaking, writing, listening and reading across all papers

lessons.title: Accommodation and Hotels
lessons.description: Hotel vocabulary, booking rooms, facilities, making complaints and dealing with problems.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for accommodation types and hotel facilities
Use je voudrais / avez-vous for polite requests and enquiries
Apply present tense and conditional for booking and asking questions
Describe problems with a room using il y a un problème and il ne fonctionne pas
method_card.title: Accommodation and Hotels
method_card.content:
This lesson covers accommodation vocabulary for holidays, including types of accommodation, hotel rooms and facilities, making bookings, and dealing with problems. The polite register is essential — use je voudrais (I would like) and avez-vous (do you have) for formal hotel interactions.

FrançaisEnglish
l'hôtel (m)the hotel
le campingthe campsite
l'auberge de jeunesse (f)the youth hostel
la chambre doublethe double room
la chambre simplethe single room
le litthe bed
la douchethe shower
le petit-déjeunerbreakfast
réserverto book / to reserve
je voudrais réserverI would like to book
avez-vous une chambre?do you have a room?
pour combien de nuits?for how many nights?
la clé / la clefthe key
il ne fonctionne pasit doesn't work
compris(e)included

Grammar focus: je voudrais and avez-vous. Je voudrais is the conditional of vouloir (to want) and is used for polite requests: Je voudrais réserver une chambre double. Avez-vous is the inverted question form of avoir (you have → do you have?): Avez-vous une chambre libre? Both structures are essential for speaking and writing at the hotel.

To report a problem, use: Il y a un problème avec… (There is a problem with…) + il/elle ne fonctionne pas (it doesn't work) or il n'y a pas de… (there is no…). For example: Il y a un problème — la douche ne fonctionne pas.

Model paragraph: Je voudrais réserver une chambre double pour deux nuits. Le petit-déjeuner est-il compris? Malheureusement, il y a un problème — la douche ne fonctionne pas. (I would like to book a double room for two nights. Is breakfast included? Unfortunately, there is a problem — the shower doesn't work.)

method_card.title: Countries, Weather and Transport
method_card.content:
This lesson covers countries with their prepositions, the weather and weather expressions, and means of transport. Use en before feminine countries, au before masculine singular countries, and aux before plural country names.

FrançaisEnglish
en France / en Espagnein/to France / Spain
au Portugal / au Japonin/to Portugal / Japan
aux États-Unis / aux Pays-Basin/to the USA / Netherlands
il fait beau / il fait chaudit's nice / it's hot
il fait froid / il fait mauvaisit's cold / it's bad weather
il pleut / il neigeit's raining / it's snowing
il y a du vent / du soleilit's windy / it's sunny
il y a des nuagesit's cloudy
en voiture / en trainby car / by train
en avion / en carby plane / by coach
à pied / à véloon foot / by bike
prendre le bus / le métroto take the bus / metro
si + présent → futurif … (si-clause for plans)
j'irais / on pourraitI would go / we could (conditional)

Grammar focus: prepositions with countries. Use en with most feminine countries and continents: en France, en Italie, en Afrique. Use au with masculine singular countries: au Portugal, au Japon, au Maroc. Use aux with plural country names: aux États-Unis, aux Pays-Bas. Note that transport uses en for enclosed vehicles (en voiture, en train, en avion) and à for open/human-powered modes (à pied, à vélo).

Weather + future plans: Link weather to activities using si + present tense → future: S'il fait beau, nous irons à la plage. (If it's nice, we'll go to the beach.) For less certain plans, use the conditional: S'il pleuvait, on pourrait visiter un musée. (If it rained, we could visit a museum.)

Model paragraph: L'année prochaine, je voudrais aller en France avec ma famille. On voyage en train et on arrive à Paris. S'il fait beau, on visitera le Louvre à pied. S'il pleut, on prendra le métro. (Next year, I would like to go to France with my family. We travel by train and arrive in Paris. If it's nice, we'll visit the Louvre on foot. If it rains, we'll take the metro.)

method_card.title: Technology and Social Media
method_card.content:
This lesson covers technology, digital devices and social media in French. A key structure is j'utilise mon/ma... pour + infinitive to say what you use a device for. You can also use ça me permet de + infinitive (it allows me to...) for more variety.

FrançaisEnglish
le portablemobile phone
l'ordinateur (m)computer
la tablettetablet
les jeux vidéo (m pl)video games
les réseaux sociaux (m pl)social networks / social media
une application (une appli)an app
envoyer un messageto send a message
téléchargerto download
se connecterto connect / log on
partagerto share
naviguer sur Internetto browse the internet
utileuseful
pratiquepractical / handy
distrayant(e)distracting
dépendant(e)addicted / dependent

Grammar focus: pour + infinitive. Use pour followed by an infinitive to express purpose. For example: J'utilise mon portable pour écouter de la musique (I use my phone to listen to music). Pour never changes and is always followed by the infinitive form of the verb, not a conjugated form.

Model paragraph: J'utilise mon portable tous les jours pour envoyer des messages et naviguer sur Internet. À mon avis, les réseaux sociaux sont utiles pour rester en contact avec mes amis, mais ils peuvent être distrayants. (I use my mobile phone every day to send messages and browse the internet. In my opinion, social networks are useful for staying in contact with my friends, but they can be distracting.)

lessons.title: My House and Home
lessons.description: Describing your house, rooms, furniture and using prepositions of place and il y a.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for rooms and furniture

Master prepositions of place and their contractions (à côté du / de la)
Describe your home in full sentences using connectives
method_card.title: My House and Home
method_card.content:
This lesson covers the rooms of the house, furniture, and how to describe where things are using prepositions of place. The key structure il y a (there is / there are) lets you describe what is in each room.

FrançaisEnglish
la maisonthe house
la cuisinethe kitchen
le salonthe living room
la chambrethe bedroom
la salle de bainsthe bathroom
la salle à mangerthe dining room
le jardinthe garden
le canapéthe sofa
l'armoire (f)the wardrobe
le litthe bed
la tablethe table
à côté denext to
suron
sousunder
dansin
en face deopposite

Grammar focus: il y a and prepositions of place. Use il y a to say what exists in a room: Dans ma chambre, il y a un lit et une armoire. Prepositions of place often contract with the definite article: à + le = au (e.g. à côté du lit), and de + le = du / de + les = des. These contractions apply to à côté de, en face de, and près de.

Model paragraph: Dans ma chambre il y a un grand lit et une armoire. Mes livres sont sur l'étagère à côté du bureau. (In my bedroom there is a large bed and a wardrobe. My books are on the shelf next to the desk.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — home and accommodation appear across speaking, listening, reading and writing every year

lessons.title: My Town and Local Area
lessons.description: Town vocabulary, describing what there is to do, using comparisons and on peut + infinitive.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for places in town (les endroits en ville)
Use il y a / il n'y a pas de to say what there is and isn't in your area
Describe your town using être and opinion phrases such as je trouve que / je pense que
Use comparatives (plus … que, moins … que) to contrast town and countryside
method_card.title: My Town and Local Area
method_card.content:
This lesson focuses on describing your town or local area in French. You will learn the names of key places, how to say what exists in your town, and how to give opinions and comparisons.

FrançaisEnglish
le cinémathe cinema
le centre sportifthe sports centre
la mairiethe town hall
les magasins (m)the shops
la médiathèquethe media library
la garethe (train) station
le marchéthe market
la piscinethe swimming pool
le parcthe park
animé(e)lively, bustling
calmequiet, calm
la campagnethe countryside
il y athere is / there are
il n'y a pas dethere is no / there are no
plus … quemore … than

Grammar focus: il y a / il n'y a pas de. Use il y a + noun (no article change) to say something exists: Il y a un cinéma dans ma ville (There is a cinema in my town). For negatives, use il n'y a pas de + noun — the article disappears completely: Il n'y a pas de piscine (There is no swimming pool). Never say il n'y a pas un/une.

To compare your town with the countryside, use the comparative: Ma ville est plus animée que la campagne (My town is livelier than the countryside). Moins … que means less … than: La campagne est moins animée que la ville.

Model paragraph: J'habite dans une petite ville dans le nord de la France. Il y a un cinéma et un centre sportif, mais il n'y a pas de piscine. Je pense que ma ville est assez animée — elle est plus animée que la campagne. (I live in a small town in the north of France. There is a cinema and a sports centre, but there is no swimming pool. I think my town is quite lively — it is livelier than the countryside.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — local area and town descriptions appear across all papers every year

lessons.title: The Environment and Global Issues

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for environmental problems (les problèmes environnementaux)

method_card.title: The Environment and Global Issues
method_card.content:
This lesson covers environmental problems and what we should do to protect the planet. Key structures for expressing obligation include il faut + infinitive (it is necessary to), on doit + infinitive (we must) and on devrait + infinitive (we should — conditional, more polite).

FrançaisEnglish
la pollutionpollution
le changement climatiqueclimate change
les déchets (m pl)waste / rubbish
l'effet de serre (m)the greenhouse effect
la déforestationdeforestation
les espèces menacées (f pl)endangered species
recyclerto recycle
économiser l'énergieto save energy
protéger la planèteto protect the planet
utiliser les transports en communto use public transport
éteindre les lumièresto turn off the lights
nuire à l'environnementto harm the environment
durable / renouvelablesustainable / renewable
la sécheressedrought
les inondations (f pl)floods

Grammar focus: il faut, on doit, on devrait + infinitive. These impersonal structures are essential for expressing obligations and recommendations. Il faut recycler (It is necessary to recycle / We must recycle), On doit économiser l'énergie (We must save energy), On devrait utiliser les transports en commun (We should use public transport). On devrait (conditional) is softer and more persuasive than on doit.

At Higher level, use il faut que + present subjunctive: Il faut que nous recyclions (We must recycle). The subjunctive of recycler → nous recyclions; other examples: il faut que nous protégions (we must protect), il faut que nous fassions (we must do).

Model paragraph: La pollution est un problème grave. Il faut recycler les déchets et économiser l'énergie. On devrait utiliser les transports en commun pour réduire le changement climatique. (Pollution is a serious problem. We must recycle waste and save energy. We should use public transport to reduce climate change.)

method_card.title: Family and Describing People
method_card.content:
In this lesson you will learn vocabulary for family members and how to describe people's appearance and personality in Spanish. Two verbs are essential: use ser for personality and permanent characteristics, and tener for physical features such as hair and eyes.

SpanishEnglish
el padre / la madrefather / mother
el hermano / la hermanabrother / sister
el abuelo / la abuelagrandfather / grandmother
el tío / la tíauncle / aunt
el padrastro / la madrastrastepfather / stepmother
el hijo / la hijason / daughter
alto/atall
bajo/ashort (height)
delgado/aslim
gordito/achubby
simpático/anice, friendly
trabajador(a)hardworking
gracioso/afunny
mayor / menorolder / younger
amablekind

Grammar focus: ser vs tener for descriptions. Use ser with adjectives describing personality: Mi hermano es gracioso (My brother is funny). Use tener with physical features involving hair and eyes: Tiene los ojos azules (She/he has blue eyes), Tiene el pelo corto (She/he has short hair). Never use estar for personality — it describes temporary states and locations, not character traits.

Adjectives must agree with the noun they describe. Adjectives ending in -o change to -a for feminine, and add -s or -as for plurals. Adjectives ending in -e (e.g. amable, inteligente) only add -s for plural — gender does not change them. Mayor and menor never change for gender.

Model paragraph: Mi padre es alto y delgado. Tiene el pelo castaño y los ojos verdes. Es muy amable y trabajador, pero a veces es un poco serio. (My father is tall and slim. He has brown hair and green eyes. He is very kind and hardworking, but sometimes he is a little serious.)

lessons.title: Friendships and Relationships
lessons.description: Talk about friendships, describe what makes a good friend, and give opinions in Spanish.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for describing friends and qualities

Use opinion phrases with infinitives to say what makes a good friend
Build richer sentences with comparatives and connectives
method_card.title: Friendships and Relationships
method_card.content:
This lesson focuses on friendships, describing qualities in a friend, and talking about relationships. The key grammar points are reflexive verbs (verbs used with a reflexive pronoun) and opinion + infinitive structures.

SpanishEnglish
el amigo / la amigafriend (m/f)
el mejor amigo / la mejor amigabest friend (m/f)
llevarse bien conto get on well with
llevarse mal conto get on badly with
pelearse conto argue / fall out with
parecerse ato look like / be similar to
confiable / de confianzatrustworthy
comprensivo/aunderstanding
lealloyal
sincero/asincere, honest
egoístaselfish
generoso/agenerous
chismoso/agossipy
apoyarto support
discutirto argue, discuss

Grammar focus: reflexive verbs. Reflexive verbs use a pronoun (me, te, se, nos, os, se) that refers back to the subject. Me llevo bien con mi mejor amiga = I get on well with my best friend. Nos peleamos a veces = We argue sometimes. Note that with llevarse the pronoun changes with the subject: me llevo, te llevas, se lleva, nos llevamos.

Grammar focus: opinion + infinitive. To say what a good friend should do, use creo que es importante + infinitive or para mí lo más importante es + infinitive. Example: Creo que es importante ser leal (I think it's important to be loyal).

Model paragraph: Mi mejor amiga se llama Sofía y nos llevamos muy bien porque es muy comprensiva y leal. A veces nos peleamos pero siempre hacemos las paces. Para mí, lo más importante en una amistad es ser sincero. (My best friend is called Sofía and we get on very well because she is very understanding and loyal. Sometimes we argue but we always make up. For me, the most important thing in a friendship is to be sincere.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — friendships and relationships appear across speaking, listening, reading and writing every year
