lessons.title: Relationships and Marriage
lessons.description: Discuss relationships, marriage and future plans using the conditional tense in Spanish.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for relationships and marriage
Master the future tense: infinitive + -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án
Use the conditional tense to express hypothetical future plans
Give and justify opinions using creo que, en mi opinión, and porque
method_card.title: Relationships and Marriage
method_card.content:
This lesson focuses on talking about relationships, marriage, and future plans. You will need the future tense (what will happen) and the conditional tense (what would happen). Both are formed from the infinitive for most verbs.

SpanishEnglish
casarseto get married
el matrimoniomarriage
la bodathe wedding
la parejathe partner / couple
vivir juntos/asto live together
comprometerseto get engaged
el divorciodivorce
divorciarseto get divorced
la relaciónthe relationship
el noviazgocourtship / engagement
soltero/asingle
casado/amarried
en mi opiniónin my opinion
me gustaríaI would like
en el futuroin the future

Grammar focus: future tense. Add the endings -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án directly to the infinitive: viviré (I will live), me casaré (I will get married). Common irregular future stems: tener → tendr-, querer → querr-, poder → podr-, haber → habr-.

Conditional tense. Add the endings -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían to the same infinitive (or irregular stem): me casaría (I would get married), viviríamos juntos (we would live together). Use the conditional for hypothetical plans and polite wishes (me gustaría = I would like).

Model paragraph: En el futuro me gustaría casarme, pero primero quiero vivir con mi pareja. Creo que el matrimonio es importante, pero el divorcio es demasiado común hoy en día. (In the future I would like to get married, but first I want to live with my partner. I think marriage is important, but divorce is too common nowadays.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — relationships and future plans appear across speaking, listening, reading and writing every year

gold.source_text: In my opinion, I would not like to get married because divorce is too common nowadays, but I would like to live with my partner in the future.

Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

wrong.encontraré: encontraré is the future indicative. Spanish does NOT use the future after cuando — use the present subjunctive: encuentre.

gaps.correct_explain: encuentre is the yo present subjunctive of encontrar. After cuando referring to a future or hypothetical event, Spanish requires the subjunctive, not the indicative.

gaps.rule: Present subjunctive in a relative clause (indefinite referent) — querer

wrong.quiere: quiere is the indicative (he/she wants). Because the referent is indefinite/hypothetical ('a partner who…'), the subjunctive quiera is needed.
wrong.querría: querría is the conditional (he/she would want). The subjunctive quiera is the correct form after an indefinite relative pronoun in this context.

gaps.correct_explain: quiera is the present subjunctive of querer. The relative clause refers to an unspecified, hypothetical partner, so the subjunctive is required.

gaps.rule: Present subjunctive after con quien referring to a hypothetical person — poder

wrong.puedo: puedo is the present indicative (I can). The subjunctive pueda is required because the partner is hypothetical and not yet identified.
wrong.podría: podría is the conditional (I could/would be able). Use the present subjunctive pueda in this type of relative clause.

gaps.correct_explain: pueda is the present subjunctive of poder. After con quien referring to a hypothetical person, the subjunctive is required.

lessons.title: Healthy Living and Lifestyle
lessons.description: Talk about health, fitness and diet using modal verbs and obligation phrases in Spanish.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for healthy and unhealthy habits, food and exercise

method_card.title: Healthy Living and Lifestyle
method_card.content:
This lesson covers healthy and unhealthy habits, food and fitness vocabulary, and how to give advice in Spanish. Three key structures express obligation and advice: deber + infinitive, hay que + infinitive, and tener que + infinitive.

SpanishEnglish
llevar una vida sanato lead a healthy life
hacer ejercicioto do exercise
comer de forma equilibradato eat a balanced diet
beber mucha aguato drink lots of water
dormir biento sleep well
el tabaco / fumartobacco / to smoke
el alcoholalcohol
la comida basurajunk food
la fruta y la verdurafruit and vegetables
estar en formato be fit / in shape
deber + infinitiveshould / ought to
hay que + infinitiveone must / you have to
tener que + infinitiveto have to
saludable / sano/ahealthy
perjudicial para la saludharmful to health

Grammar focus: giving advice. Use deber conjugated for the person: Debes comer más fruta (You should eat more fruit). Hay que is impersonal (no subject) and never changes: Hay que hacer ejercicio todos los días (You have to exercise every day). Tener que changes for person: Tengo que dormir más (I have to sleep more).

Model paragraph: Para llevar una vida sana, hay que hacer ejercicio regularmente y comer de forma equilibrada. Además, debes evitar la comida basura y beber mucha agua. (To lead a healthy life, you have to exercise regularly and eat a balanced diet. Also, you should avoid junk food and drink lots of water.)

lessons.description: Master food and drink vocabulary, describe mealtimes and express food preferences in Spanish.

method_card.title: Food, Drink and Mealtimes
method_card.content:
This lesson covers food and drink vocabulary, the three main meals of the day, and how to express likes and dislikes using gustar and encantar. The key grammar rule: the verb agrees with the thing liked, not the person doing the liking.

SpanishEnglish
el desayunobreakfast
la comidalunch (main midday meal)
la cenadinner / supper
el panbread
la frutafruit
las verdurasvegetables
la carnemeat
el pescadofish
el arrozrice
los dulcessweets / sweet foods
la comida basurajunk food
saludable / sano/ahealthy
poco sano/aunhealthy
me gusta / me gustanI like (singular / plural)
me encanta / me encantanI love (singular / plural)

Grammar focus: gustar and encantar agreement. In Spanish, gustar and encantar agree with the noun that follows, not the subject. Use the singular form when followed by a singular noun or infinitive: Me gusta la fruta (I like fruit). Use the plural form when followed by a plural noun: Me gustan las verduras (I like vegetables). The indirect object pronoun changes for person: me (I), te (you), le (he/she).

Model paragraph: En el desayuno como cereales y bebo un vaso de leche. Me encanta la fruta pero no me gustan las verduras. Creo que es importante comer de forma sana. (For breakfast I eat cereal and drink a glass of milk. I love fruit but I don't like vegetables. I think it is important to eat healthily.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — food, drink and mealtimes appear across all four papers every year

gold.source_text: My sister loves vegetables and always eats fruit for breakfast, but she doesn't like sweet foods because they are unhealthy.
model_answers: A mi hermana le encantan las verduras y siempre come fruta en el desayuno, pero no le gustan los dulces porque son poco sanos.

Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

distractor_labels.cenan: wrong person — cenan is ellos/they; you need cenamos (nosotros/we)

lessons.title: Body Parts, Illness and Ailments
lessons.description: Learn body parts vocabulary, describe symptoms and practise using 'me duele' at the doctor's.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for parts of the body and common illnesses
Master me duele / me duelen (agreement with singular/plural nouns) to say what hurts
Use tener + noun and estar + adjective to describe illness and symptoms
Practice giving and following advice at the doctor or pharmacy
method_card.title: Body Parts, Illness and Ailments
method_card.content:
This lesson covers body parts, illness vocabulary, and how to talk about symptoms and seek medical help. Two key structures describe pain: me duele + singular noun and me duelen + plural noun — these are like gustar and must agree in number with the body part, not the speaker.

SpanishEnglish
la cabezahead
la gargantathroat
el estómagostomach
la espaldaback
el pechochest
la rodillaknee
el tobilloankle
los oídosears (inner)
me duele / me duelenit hurts / they hurt (to me)
tener fiebreto have a fever
tener tosto have a cough
estar resfriado/ato have a cold
estar enfermo/ato be ill
el médico / la médicadoctor (m/f)
la farmaciachemist / pharmacy

Grammar focus: me duele / me duelen. Me duele is used before a singular body part: Me duele la cabeza (My head hurts / I have a headache). Me duelen is used before a plural body part: Me duelen los pies (My feet hurt). The verb agrees with the body part, not the person — exactly like me gusta vs me gustan. You can also say tener dolor de + body part: Tengo dolor de cabeza (I have a headache).

Model paragraph: Me encuentro muy mal hoy. Me duele la garganta y tengo fiebre. Creo que estoy resfriada. Voy a ir a la farmacia para comprar medicamentos. (I feel very unwell today. My throat hurts and I have a fever. I think I have a cold. I am going to go to the pharmacy to buy some medicine.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — illness, body parts and medical situations appear across speaking, listening, reading and writing

gaps.rule: Present subjunctive after aconsejar que (imperfect subjunctive — advice/recommendation)

wrong.me quedé: me quedé is the preterite. After aconsejar que, you need the subjunctive → me quedara / me quedase.
wrong.me quedaré: me quedaré is the future. After a verb of recommendation/advice, use the subjunctive → me quedara.

gaps.correct_explain: me quedara is the imperfect subjunctive of quedarse. After aconsejar que (to advise that), Spanish requires the subjunctive.

gaps.rule: Imperfect subjunctive of volver in a subordinate clause after que

wrong.volví: volví is the preterite indicative (I returned). After the indirect advice clause, use subjunctive → volviera / volviese.
wrong.volveré: volveré is the future indicative. The subjunctive is required here → volviera.

gaps.correct_explain: volviera is the imperfect subjunctive of volver. The clause following the doctor's advice requires the subjunctive.

gaps.rule: Imperfect subjunctive of sentirse after hasta que (until)

wrong.sentía: sentía is the imperfect indicative. After hasta que when referring to an uncertain future event in a past context, use the subjunctive → sintiera.
wrong.sentiré: sentiré is the future indicative. In subordinate clauses after hasta que (past context), the subjunctive is needed → sintiera.

gaps.correct_explain: sintiera is the imperfect subjunctive of sentirse. After hasta que in a past context, the subjunctive is required.

method_card.title: Drugs, Smoking and Alcohol
method_card.content:
This lesson covers the vocabulary and structures needed to discuss smoking, alcohol and drugs in Spanish — why people start, the health risks, and how to give advice. The key grammar structures for giving advice are deber + infinitive, no se debe + infinitive, hay que + infinitive and es importante + infinitive.

SpanishEnglish
fumarto smoke
el tabaco / el cigarrillotobacco / cigarette
el alcohol / beber alcoholalcohol / to drink alcohol
las drogas / las drogas ilegalesdrugs / illegal drugs
la adicción / ser adicto/aaddiction / to be addicted
la presión de grupopeer pressure
es perjudicial para la saludit is harmful to health
dañino/a para la saluddamaging to health
provoca enfermedadesit causes illness / diseases
el cáncer de pulmónlung cancer
dejar de fumarto stop smoking
no se debe + infinitiveone should not / you should not
es importante + infinitiveit is important to
intentarto try
evitarto avoid

Grammar focus: giving advice and expressing obligation. Deber is conjugated for the subject: Debes evitar el alcohol (You should avoid alcohol). No se debe is impersonal — it never changes: No se debe fumar en lugares públicos (You should not smoke in public places). Hay que is also impersonal: Hay que cuidar la salud (You have to look after your health). Es importante is followed directly by an infinitive: Es importante hacer ejercicio (It is important to exercise).

Model paragraph: Fumar es muy perjudicial para la salud porque provoca el cáncer de pulmón y la adicción. Mucha gente empieza a fumar por la presión de grupo. lessons.title: School Subjects and Opinions
lessons.description: Master school subjects vocabulary, give opinions with reasons and use comparatives and superlatives.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for school subjects and opinion phrases
Use porque es + adjective to give reasons for your opinions
Master comparatives: más/menos ... que to compare subjects
Use se me da bien/mal to describe ability, and express favourite subjects with preferences
method_card.title: School Subjects and Opinions
method_card.content:
This lesson covers school subjects, how to give opinions about them, and how to compare subjects. Two key structures are essential: porque es + adjective (because it is + adjective) to explain opinions, and más/menos ... que (more/less ... than) to make comparisons.

SpanishEnglish
las matemáticasmaths
las cienciasscience
el inglésEnglish
la historiahistory
la geografíageography
el arteart
la educación físicaPE / physical education
la informáticaICT / computing
la músicamusic
útil / inútiluseful / useless
aburrido/aboring
interesanteinteresting
difícil / fácildifficult / easy
se me da bienI am good at it
se me da malI am bad at it

Grammar focus: comparatives. To say something is more than something else, use más + adjective + que: Las ciencias son más difíciles que el arte (Science is more difficult than art). For less, use menos + adjective + que: La historia es menos aburrida que la geografía (History is less boring than geography). The adjective must agree with the subject in gender and number.

Model paragraph: Mi asignatura favorita es la educación física porque es muy divertida y se me da bien. Sin embargo, no me gustan las matemáticas porque son más difíciles que las ciencias y se me da mal. (My favourite subject is PE because it is very fun and I am good at it. However, I don't like maths because it is more difficult than science and I am bad at it.)

Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

lessons.title: Teachers, School Day and Facilities
lessons.description: Describe teachers and school facilities, talk about your school day and tell the time in Spanish.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for school facilities, teachers and the timetable
Master telling the time with a las... (at...) and time expressions
Use hay / no hay to say what your school has and doesn't have
Build daily routine sentences with reflexive verbs: me levanto, me despierto, empiezo
method_card.title: Teachers, School Day and Facilities
method_card.content:
This lesson covers the school day, timetable and facilities in Spanish. Key structures include telling the time, using hay / no hay to describe what exists, and reflexive verbs for your daily routine.

SpanishEnglish
el instituto / el colegiosecondary school
el horariothe timetable
la bibliotecathe library
el gimnasiothe gym
el laboratoriothe laboratory
la sala de informáticathe IT room / computer room
el patiothe playground / courtyard
el comedorthe canteen / dining hall
el/la profesor(a)teacher
estricto/astrict
simpático/anice, friendly
aburrido/aboring
a las ocho y mediaat half past eight
me levantoI get up
empiezo las clasesI start lessons

Grammar focus: telling the time and reflexive verbs. Use a las + time to say when things happen: Las clases empiezan a las nueve (Lessons start at nine). For half past use y media: a las ocho y media (at half past eight). Reflexive verbs need a pronoun before the conjugated verb: me levanto (I get up), te levantas (you get up), se levanta (he/she gets up).

Model paragraph: Me levanto a las siete y empiezo las clases a las nueve menos cuarto. En mi instituto hay un gimnasio grande y una biblioteca moderna. Los profesores son bastante simpáticos pero algunos son muy estrictos. (I get up at seven and I start lessons at a quarter to nine. In my school there is a big gym and a modern library. The teachers are quite nice but some are very strict.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — school life and daily routine appear across all four papers every year

lessons.title: School Rules, Homework and Future Plans
lessons.description: Learn school rules with 'se debe', discuss homework and use the future tense for plans after school.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for school rules, uniform and homework
Master está prohibido, se debe, hay que and no se permite to talk about rules
Use voy a + infinitive and the simple future tense to talk about future plans
Use quiero and me gustaría + infinitive to express wishes and ambitions
method_card.title: School Rules, Homework and Future Plans
method_card.content:
This lesson covers school rules, uniform vocabulary, homework and future study or work plans. Two sets of grammar structures are essential: expressing rules with está prohibido / se debe / hay que / no se permite, and expressing future plans with voy a + infinitive, the simple future tense, and quiero / me gustaría + infinitive.

SpanishEnglish
las normas del colegioschool rules
el uniforme escolarschool uniform
está prohibido + infinitiveit is forbidden to
se debe + infinitiveone should / you must
hay que + infinitiveyou have to
no se permite + infinitiveit is not allowed to
los debereshomework
hacer los deberesto do homework
llegar tardeto arrive late
respetar a los profesoresto respect teachers
usar el móvil en claseto use a mobile phone in class
voy a estudiarI am going to study
estudiaré / trabajaréI will study / I will work
quiero + infinitiveI want to
me gustaría + infinitiveI would like to

Grammar focus: expressing rules and future plans. To state rules, use impersonal structures: Está prohibido usar el móvil en clase (It is forbidden to use a mobile phone in class). Se debe respetar a los profesores (You should respect teachers). No se permite llegar tarde (Arriving late is not allowed). For future plans, voy a + infinitive is used for near or decided plans: Voy a estudiar medicina (I am going to study medicine). The simple future tense adds endings to the infinitive: trabajaré (I will work), vivirá (he/she will live). Quiero and me gustaría both take an infinitive: Me gustaría ser médico (I would like to be a doctor).

Model paragraph: En mi colegio hay muchas normas. Está prohibido usar el móvil en clase y se debe llevar uniforme todos los días. En el futuro, me gustaría ir a la universidad y estudiaré Derecho porque quiero ser abogado. (In my school there are many rules. It is forbidden to use a mobile phone in class and you must wear uniform every day. In the future, I would like to go to university and I will study Law because I want to be a lawyer.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — school life and future plans appear across all four papers every year

gaps.rule: Imperfect tense in reported speech — estaba prohibido

wrong.está: está is present tense. After dijo que (said that) the tense shifts to imperfect → estaba.
wrong.estuvo: estuvo is preterite (it was/was for a completed event). Rules are ongoing states → imperfect estaba.

gaps.correct_explain: estaba is the imperfect of estar. In reported speech, the present está shifts back to the imperfect estaba: El director dijo que estaba prohibido...

gaps.rule: Present subjunctive in prohibitions — estar prohibido que + subjunctive

wrong.usan: usan is the indicative (they use). After prohibido que you must use the subjunctive → usaran.
wrong.usarán: usarán is the future tense (they will use). After prohibido que the subjunctive is required → usaran.

gaps.correct_explain: usaran (or usasen) is the imperfect subjunctive of usar. After estaba prohibido que (it was forbidden that), Spanish requires the subjunctive mood.

wrong.es: es que does not express obligation. Use hay que + infinitive for 'one must'.
wrong.tienes: tienes que means 'you have to' but is personal. Hay que is impersonal and more formal for stating rules.

gaps.correct_explain: hay que is an impersonal expression meaning 'you have to'. It never changes form.

wrong.quiere: quiere is he/she wants. The subject is yo, so use quiero.
wrong.querería: querería is the conditional (I would want). Use quiero for a present desire.

gaps.correct_explain: quiero is the yo form of querer (to want). It is followed directly by an infinitive.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: For a planned near-future action, use ir a + infinitive: Voy a estudiar en la universidad. Voy is the yo form of ir.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: For a more distant or certain future, use the simple future tense. Add the future endings to the infinitive: trabajar → trabajaré (I will work). Ending for yo = -é.

steps.label: Answer

worked_examples.question: How do you say 'I am going to study at university' and 'I will work in Spain'?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: When está prohibido que is followed by a different subject, the verb after que must be in the subjunctive. Compare: Está prohibido usar el móvil (same implied subject, infinitive) vs. Está prohibido que los alumnos usen el móvil (different subject → subjunctive usen).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: The present subjunctive of usar (yo form: quite → quite → use) gives: yo use, tú uses, él/ella use, nosotros usemos, vosotros uséis, ellos usen.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Está prohibido que los alumnos usen el móvil en clase. (It is forbidden for students to use the mobile phone in class.)

lessons.title: Free-Time Activities and Hobbies
lessons.description: Essential vocabulary for hobbies and sports, plus using the present tense to say what you do.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for free-time activities and hobbies
Master gustar and encantar with infinitives and plural nouns
Use frequency adverbs to say how often you do activities
Build extended sentences with opinions using porque
method_card.title: Free-Time Activities and Hobbies
method_card.content:
This lesson covers free-time activities and hobbies. The key structures are me gusta / me encanta (I like / I love) followed by an infinitive, and the present tense of common activity verbs.

SpanishEnglish
los ratos libresfree time
los pasatiemposhobbies
jugar al fútbolto play football
hacer deporteto do sport
salir con amigosto go out with friends
escuchar músicato listen to music
ver la televisiónto watch television
leer librosto read books
tocar la guitarrato play the guitar
navegar por internetto browse the internet
a menudooften
todos los díasevery day
los fines de semanaat weekends
me gusta / me encantaI like / I love
no me gusta nadaI don't like at all

Grammar focus: gustar and encantar. These verbs work back-to-front in Spanish: the thing you like is actually the subject. Use me gusta + singular noun or infinitive, and me gustan + plural noun. For example: Me gusta jugar al fútbol (I like playing football) — but Me gustan los deportes (I like sports). Encantar follows the same pattern and means to love.

Model paragraph: En mis ratos libres me encanta escuchar música y salgo con mis amigos los fines de semana. Juego al fútbol todos los días porque es muy emocionante. (In my free time I love listening to music and I go out with my friends at weekends. I play football every day because it is very exciting.)

lessons.title: Music, Film and Television
lessons.description: Giving opinions about music, films and TV using me encanta, me aburre and key adjectives.

steps: Learn key vocabulary for types of music, films and TV programmes
Use prefiero, me encanta and lo bueno/malo es que to express opinions and preferences
Use escuchar and ver with direct objects and time expressions
Master the preterite tense to describe a film or programme you watched
method_card.title: Music, Film and Television
method_card.content:
This lesson covers music genres, film types and television programmes, and the language you need to express opinions and talk about media you have watched or listened to.

SpanishEnglish
la música pop / el rap / el rockpop music / rap / rock
la música clásicaclassical music
la canción / el cantantesong / singer
el grupo / la bandaband / group
la película de acciónaction film
la película de terrorhorror film
la comedia / el dramacomedy / drama
la serie / el programaseries / programme
las noticiasthe news
el documentaldocumentary
escuchar músicato listen to music
ver una películato watch a film
prefiero / me encanta(n)I prefer / I love
lo bueno / lo malo es quethe good / bad thing is that
el protagonista / el actormain character / actor

Grammar focus: opinions and comparatives. Use prefiero + infinitive to say what you prefer doing: Prefiero escuchar música pop (I prefer listening to pop music). Use me encanta with a singular noun and me encantan with a plural noun: Me encanta el rock; me encantan las comedias. To give reasons, use lo bueno/malo es que + a clause: Lo bueno es que la música me relaja. For comparatives: más ... que (more ... than) and menos ... que (less ... than).

Preterite for describing what you watched/listened to. Use the preterite to say what you watched: Vi una película de terror (I watched a horror film), Escuché un álbum nuevo (I listened to a new album). Irregular preterites: ver → vi/viste/vio; ir → fui/fuiste/fue.

Model paragraph: El fin de semana pasado vi una comedia con mis amigos. Lo bueno es que fue muy divertida y nos reímos mucho. Prefiero las comedias a las películas de terror porque me encantan las escenas graciosas. (Last weekend I watched a comedy with my friends. The good thing is that it was very entertaining and we laughed a lot. I prefer comedies to horror films because I love funny scenes.)

method_card.title: Sport and Exercise
method_card.content:
This lesson covers sports and exercise, expressing how often you train, giving opinions, and talking about a match or competition in the past. Two key structures distinguish types of sport: use jugar a for competitive team and ball sports, and hacer for individual activities and exercise.

SpanishEnglish
el fútbol / el baloncestofootball / basketball
el tenis / el balonmanotennis / handball
la nataciónswimming
el ciclismocycling
el atletismoathletics
el gimnasiothe gym
entrenar / el entrenamientoto train / training
el partido / la competiciónmatch / competition
ganar / perder / empatarto win / to lose / to draw
el equipo / el jugadorteam / player
mantenerse en formato stay fit / keep in shape
dos veces a la semanatwice a week
saludable / sanohealthy
emocionante / aburridoexciting / boring

Grammar focus: jugar a vs hacer. Use jugar a + definite article + sport for competitive sports played with a ball or opponent: juego al fútbol (I play football), juegas al tenis (you play tennis). Use hacer + sport noun for individual exercise and activities: hago natación (I swim), hace atletismo (he/she does athletics). Never say juego natación or hago fútbol.

Model paragraph: Juego al fútbol dos veces a la semana porque me encanta y es muy emocionante. El fin de semana pasado jugué un partido con mi equipo y ganamos tres a uno. Hacer deporte me ayuda a mantenerme en forma. (I play football twice a week because I love it and it is very exciting. Last weekend I played a match with my team and we won three-one. Doing sport helps me to stay fit.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — sport and keeping fit appear across speaking, listening, reading and writing papers every year

method_card.title: Eating Out and Restaurant Conversations
method_card.content:
This lesson covers eating out at a restaurant or café. You will need vocabulary for the menu, polite ordering phrases, and the preterite tense to describe a meal you had in the past.

SpanishEnglish
el restaurante / el caférestaurant / café
el menú / la cartaset menu / à la carte menu
los platosthe dishes / courses
el primer platothe starter
el segundo platothe main course
el postredessert
la cuentathe bill
el camarero / la camarerawaiter / waitress
quisiera / me poneI would like / can you give me (lit.)
para mífor me
¿Qué recomienda?What do you recommend?
estaba rico / deliciosoit was delicious (imperfect for taste)
pedí / comí / bebíI ordered / I ate / I drank (preterite)
sin / conwithout / with
¿Me puede traer…?Can you bring me…?

Grammar focus: polite ordering and the preterite. To order politely, use quisiera (conditional of querer — I would like) or para mí (for me): Quisiera la sopa, por favor. To describe the meal afterwards, use the preterite: Pedí la paella (I ordered the paella), Comí el pescado (I ate the fish). For opinions on how something tasted, use the imperfect estaba: Estaba muy rico (It was very tasty). This is because estar describes a temporary state (how something tasted at that moment), not a permanent quality.

Model paragraph: Ayer fui a un restaurante con mi familia. De primer plato pedí la sopa y de segundo comí el pollo asado. Estaba riquísimo. Al final pedimos la cuenta y pagamos con tarjeta. (Yesterday I went to a restaurant with my family. For a starter I ordered the soup and for a main I ate the roast chicken. It was absolutely delicious. At the end we asked for the bill and paid by card.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — eating out appears regularly across speaking role plays, listening tasks and writing

lessons.title: Spanish Festivals and Celebrations
lessons.description: Key Spanish festivals — Las Fallas, La Tomatina, Semana Santa and Día de los Muertos.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for festivals and celebrations
Master the preterite tense for regular and irregular verbs
Practise describing what happens at specific festivals
Use time expressions like el año pasado and el fin de semana pasado
method_card.title: Spanish Festivals and Celebrations
method_card.content:
This lesson covers major festivals in the Spanish-speaking world. You will learn vocabulary for describing what happens at festivals, and practise the preterite tense to talk about past celebrations.

SpanishEnglish
la fiesta / el festivalfestival / celebration
la festividadfestivity
los fuegos artificialesfireworks
el desfileparade / procession
la procesiónreligious procession
la tradicióntradition
las hoguerasbonfires
la calaveraskull (Day of the Dead)
los tomatestomatoes
celebrar / celebramosto celebrate / we celebrated
disfrazarseto dress up / wear a costume
tirarto throw
la ofrendaoffering (altar offering)
el ambienteatmosphere
la Semana SantaHoly Week (Easter)

Grammar focus: the preterite tense. Use the preterite to describe completed past actions. Regular -ar verbs: celebr- → celebré (I celebrated), celebramos (we celebrated), celebró (he/she celebrated). Irregular stems: ir/ser → fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos. Common festival sentence: Fuimos a Las Fallas y tiramos petardos.

Model paragraph: El año pasado celebramos la Semana Santa en Sevilla. Vimos una procesión impresionante y comimos torrijas tradicionales. ¡El ambiente fue increíble! (Last year we celebrated Holy Week in Seville. We saw an impressive procession and ate traditional torrijas. The atmosphere was incredible!)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — festivals and cultural celebrations appear across reading, listening, speaking and writing papers

Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for celebrations and Spanish traditions
Use soler + infinitive to describe what your family usually does
Use the imperfect tense with de niño/a to describe childhood customs
Build extended answers combining present habits with past memories
method_card.title: Customs and Traditions
method_card.content:
This lesson covers Spanish customs and family celebrations. You will learn vocabulary for key festivities and traditional food, and practise two essential grammar structures: soler + infinitive (to usually do something) and the imperfect tense for habitual past actions.

SpanishEnglish
la costumbrethe custom / tradition
la tradiciónthe tradition
el cumpleañosthe birthday
la bodathe wedding
la NavidadChristmas
la NocheviejaNew Year's Eve
las doce uvasthe twelve grapes
los fuegos artificialesfireworks
el turrónnougat (traditional Christmas sweet)
el roscón de ReyesThree Kings' ring cake
la paellapaella
reunirse con la familiato get together with the family
celebrarto celebrate
soler + infinitiveto usually do (something)
de niño/aas a child

Grammar focus: soler + infinitive and the imperfect. Use soler + infinitive to express what someone usually does: Solemos comer paella en familia (We usually eat paella as a family). The present tense forms are: suelo, sueles, suele, solemos, soléis, suelen. For habitual past actions, use the imperfect tense with time phrases like de niño/a (as a child) or cuando era pequeño/a (when I was young): De niño, celebrábamos la Nochevieja con toda la familia (As a child, we used to celebrate New Year's Eve with the whole family).

Model paragraph: En mi familia solemos celebrar la Navidad juntos. De niña, siempre comíamos turrón y abríamos los regalos el veinticinco de diciembre. En Nochevieja nos reunimos con los abuelos y tomamos las doce uvas cuando suenan las campanadas. (In my family we usually celebrate Christmas together. As a child, we always used to eat nougat and open presents on the 25th of December. On New Year's Eve we get together with the grandparents and eat the twelve grapes when the bells chime.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — traditions and celebrations appear in speaking, writing, listening and reading tasks every year

gold.source_text: When I was a child, we used to celebrate New Year's Eve together. My grandmother would cook a big dinner and we always ate the twelve grapes when the bells chimed at midnight.
model_answers: Cuando era niña, celebrábamos la Nochevieja juntos. Mi abuela cocinaba una cena grande y siempre comíamos las doce uvas cuando sonaban las campanadas a medianoche.

Accept any grammatically correct translation that conveys the same meaning. Check: consistent use of the imperfect for habitual/descriptive past, correct imperfect conjugations (-aba/-ía endings), noun genders, word order. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

lessons.title: Celebrity Culture and Role Models
lessons.description: Talking about celebrities, role models and social media influence using key opinion structures.

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for describing celebrities and role models
Master relative clauses with que to link ideas about the same person
Express opinions about why someone inspires you using porque and infinitives
Use a range of adjectives with correct gender agreement
method_card.title: Celebrity Culture and Role Models
method_card.content:
This lesson covers celebrities and role models. The key structure is the relative clause with que: una persona que admiro (a person whom I admire). You will also practise describing qualities and expressing opinions about famous people.

SpanishEnglish
un modelo a seguira role model
un/una famoso/aa celebrity
admirarto admire
inspirarto inspire
la famafame
el éxitosuccess
influyenteinfluential
talentoso/atalented
generoso/agenerous
comprometido/acommitted, dedicated
la influenciainfluence
los valoresvalues
una persona que admiroa person I admire
me inspira ahe/she inspires me to
tiene mucho talentohe/she is very talented

Grammar focus: relative clauses with que. Use que to link two ideas about the same noun: una persona que admiro mucho (a person I admire a lot). The verb after que agrees with the original noun, not with que itself. You can extend the clause: Es un deportista que trabaja muy duro y que inspira a mucha gente (He is a sportsperson who works very hard and who inspires many people).

Model paragraph: Mi modelo a seguir es una cantante que tiene mucho talento y que es muy generosa. Me inspira a trabajar duro y a nunca rendirme. (My role model is a singer who is very talented and who is very generous. She inspires me to work hard and never give up.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — celebrities and role models appear in speaking and writing tasks every year

lessons.title: Social Media and Online Life
lessons.description: Social media vocabulary, screen time debates and forming opinions about online life in Spanish.

steps: Learn key vocabulary for online activities and social media
Use para + infinitive to explain the purpose of online activities
Express advantages and disadvantages using las ventajas / los inconvenientes
Use the present subjunctive after no creo que to give opinions at Higher level
method_card.title: Social Media and Online Life
method_card.content:
This lesson covers the vocabulary and grammar you need to discuss social media platforms, online activities and the advantages and disadvantages of life online.

SpanishEnglish
las redes socialessocial media / social networks
subir fotosto upload photos
chatearto chat online
navegar por internetto browse the internet
compartirto share
publicarto post / publish
seguir a alguiento follow someone
el seguidor / la seguidorafollower
el perfilprofile
la contraseñapassword
las ventajasthe advantages
los inconvenientesthe disadvantages
la seguridad en líneaonline safety
el acoso cibernéticocyberbullying
adicto/a a las pantallasaddicted to screens

Grammar focus: para + infinitive. Use para + infinitive to express purpose (in order to): Uso las redes sociales para comunicarme con mis amigos (I use social media in order to communicate with my friends). This structure appears frequently in writing and speaking tasks when justifying your use of technology.

Higher grammar: present subjunctive after no creo que. After no creo que (I don't think that), the following verb must be in the present subjunctive: No creo que sea bueno pasar tanto tiempo en línea (I don't think it is good to spend so much time online). The subjunctive form of ser is sea (él/ella/ello).

Model paragraph: Uso las redes sociales para chatear con mis amigos y subir fotos. Las ventajas son que es fácil mantenerse en contacto, pero uno de los inconvenientes es el acoso cibernético. No creo que sea bueno compartir información personal en línea. (I use social media to chat with my friends and upload photos. The advantages are that it is easy to stay in contact, but one of the disadvantages is cyberbullying. I don't think it is good to share personal information online.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — technology and social media appear across all four papers every year

gold.source_text: I think that social media can be useful for communicating with family, but I spend too much time on my phone and that is not good for my health.

gaps.rule: Present subjunctive — ser (sea) after no creo que

wrong.es: es is the indicative (normal present tense). After no creo que, you must use the subjunctive → sea.
wrong.será: será is the future tense. After no creo que, use the present subjunctive → sea.

gaps.correct_explain: sea is the present subjunctive of ser. After no creo que, Spanish requires the subjunctive mood.

gaps.rule: First person singular of creer — creo

wrong.cree: cree is the él/ella form. The subject is yo (I) → creo.
wrong.creen: creen is the ellos/ellas form (they think). First person singular = creo.

gaps.correct_explain: creo is the yo form of creer in the present tense.

gaps.rule: Present subjunctive — ser (sea) after no creo que (second instance)

wrong.es: es is indicative. The subjunctive is required here after no creo que → sea.
wrong.eres: eres is the tú indicative form. Use third person subjunctive sea here.

gaps.correct_explain: sea is again the present subjunctive of ser, triggered by no creo que.

bronze.question: Match the Spanish words to their English meaning
Match the Spanish expressions to their English meaning

wrong.a: a is used with movement verbs (e.g. voy a hablar), not with usar to express purpose.
wrong.por: por is used for reasons/causes in the past or general motives, not for purpose with an infinitive. Use para + infinitive.

gaps.correct_explain: para + infinitive means 'in order to'. It expresses the purpose of an action.

wrong.suba: suba is a subjunctive form. After para, use the infinitive: subir.
wrong.subiendo: subiendo is the gerund. After para, always use the infinitive: subir.

gaps.correct_explain: subir is the infinitive meaning 'to upload'. After para, always use the infinitive.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence

wrong.problemas: problemas means problems. The correct word for advantages is ventajas.
wrong.inconvenientes: inconvenientes means disadvantages. Easy contact is a positive thing → use ventajas.

gaps.correct_explain: ventajas means advantages. Una de las ventajas = one of the advantages.

wrong.quedar: quedar means 'to meet up' or 'to remain'. Use mantenerse for 'to stay in contact'.
wrong.mantener: mantener is the non-reflexive infinitive. The set phrase is mantenerse en contacto (to stay in touch).

gaps.correct_explain: mantenerse is the reflexive infinitive meaning 'to keep/stay'. Mantenerse en contacto = to stay in contact.

gaps.rule: Present tense — nosotros form of pasar

wrong.pasan: pasan is the ellos/ellas form. The subject is mis amigos y yo = we → pasamos.
wrong.pasáis: pasáis is the vosotros form (you all). Mis amigos y yo = nosotros → pasamos.

gaps.correct_explain: pasamos is the nosotros form of pasar in the present tense.

wrong.gustan: gustan is used with plural nouns. An infinitive is treated as singular → gusta.
wrong.gustamos: gustamos does not exist as a form of gustar. This verb works differently — use nos gusta.

gaps.correct_explain: gusta agrees with the infinitive mantenernos. When gustar is followed by an infinitive, always use the singular gusta.

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: Uso las redes sociales para subir fotos y chatear.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Look at the structure after para. In Spanish, para must always be followed by an infinitive.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: compartido ends in -ido, which is a past participle, not an infinitive. The infinitive of this verb is compartir.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: The error is compartido — change it to compartir (the infinitive). Correct: para compartir información.

worked_examples.question: Spot the error: Uso el móvil para compartido información con mis amigos.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Start with no creo que (I don't think that). This phrase always triggers the present subjunctive in the next clause.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: The verb 'to be' is ser. Its present subjunctive (él/ella/ello form) is sea. Then add the rest: bueno pasar tanto tiempo en línea.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: No creo que sea bueno pasar tanto tiempo en línea.
